title: AWS Certificate Manager supports switching from e-mail to DNS validation
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with AWS Certificate Manager supports switching from e-mail to DNS validation
body_text: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) now enables you to change the domain validation method on your existing ACM issued public TLS certificates from e-mail to DNS, without reissuing the certificate or changing its existing Amazon Resource Name (ARN). Due to the Certification Authority/Browser (CA/B) Forum's mandated deprecation of email-based domain validation for publicly trusted certificates, effective March 15, 2028, ACM will phase out its support for email validation throughout 2027. ACM will no longer issue email-validated certificates starting March 31 2027, and stop renewing email-validated certificates on September 30 2027. More details on ACM's deprecation of email validation can be found on the AWS Security Blog . By switching to DNS validation now, you can transition ahead of that deadline and enable fully automated renewals through DNS validated certificates. Your certificate ARN remains unchanged after switching from e-mail to DNS validation, so existing ARN references in your CI/CD pipelines, load balancer configurations, and other AWS service integrations continue to work without modification. To switch the validation method, use the ACM console or the UpdateCertificateOptions API. ACM provides a CNAME record for each domain in the certificate (the same mechanism used when provisioning new certificates with DNS validation) and you have up to 72 hours to add the records to your DNS configuration. You can monitor the validation status of each domain via the console or the ListCertificateDomainValidations API. We recommend DNS validation for new certificates, and HTTP validation for Amazon CloudFront distributions.. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where ACM certificates are available. To get started, refer to Migrating from email to DNS validation in the AWS Certificate Manager User Guide.

title: 3 Best Fleet Cards with Maintenance Options Built-In
summary: Compare 3 fleet cards with maintenance options built in. AtoB helps manage fuel, maintenance, and driver spend while saving 42¢/gal on average.
body_text: Most fleets manage fuel and maintenance with separate payment methods, creating reconciliation gaps that hide the true cost of operating each vehicle. Fleet cards with built-in maintenance options help consolidate fuel, repairs, parts, and other vehicle-related expenses into a single payment solution with unified controls and reporting. This guide explains what to look for in a fleet card with maintenance capabilities and compares three programs designed to simplify fleet spending. Beyond fuel purchases, today's fleet cards can also help businesses manage maintenance, parts, reporting, and other vehicle-related expenses from a single platform. What to Look for in a Fleet Card with Maintenance Options A maintenance-enabled fleet card should support repair purchases, parts purchases, fuel transactions, and approved vehicle expenses under one control framework. The right fuel card helps fleet operators reduce fuel costs while simplifying fleet expense management across every vehicle. Here is what to look for: Built-in Visibility Across Fuel, Repairs, and Driver Expenses True cost-per-vehicle tracking requires seeing fuel purchases, repair invoices, parts transactions, and fuel data in a single view. Bringing this information together helps fleet operators compare fuel usage, repair frequency, maintenance costs, and the amount of fuel consumed by each vehicle. Fleet cards that allow businesses to make vehicle-related purchases anywhere Mastercard is accepted support maintenance purchases at many repair shops, parts suppliers, tire dealers, and truck stop service centers. Unlike some branded fuel card providers, broader acceptance gives fleets greater flexibility when job sites, routes, or truck stop networks change. Platforms like AtoB consolidate fuel, maintenance, parts, and driver spending into one dashboard, helping businesses lower fuel expenses while improving visibility into the fleet's operating costs. Controls That Prevent Unauthorized Fuel and Maintenance Spend Without proper spend controls, a maintenance-enabled fleet card functions much like a standard business credit card or business charge card, making it more difficult to monitor and control employee spending. Fleet managers need granular controls that help protect margins while still giving drivers flexibility. Key control types to evaluate: Merchant category restrictions – Limit purchases by fuel type, repairs, parts, and other approved vehicle expenses Per-transaction caps – Set dollar limits by expense type to flag unusual charges Driver-level authorization – Assign cards to specific drivers with individual rules Vendor whitelisting – Approve or block specific repair shops and parts suppliers These capabilities help businesses purchase fuel, manage maintenance costs, and reduce unauthorized spending across the fleet. Reporting That Supports Preventive Fleet Maintenance Management Fleet cards capture odometer readings and fuel data during each fuel transaction. Combined with GPS and telematics data, this information can support preventive maintenance scheduling, International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA) reporting, and better visibility into fuel volume across the fleet. Declining fuel efficiency or higher fuel consumption than expected may indicate maintenance issues before they become costly repairs. When a vehicle suddenly uses more fuel per mile, it may indicate engine problems, tire wear, or other fleet maintenance needs. Reporting tools help businesses reduce fuel waste, lower fuel expenses, and improve long-term operating efficiency while providing better insight into monthly fuel trends. Up to 42¢ off per gallon* at participating truck stops. WEX Fleet Card Fuel management Participating maintenance and fuel network. Savings vary by program and network participation. Coast Fleet Card Fleet expense management Limited to participating network locations. Volume-tiered rebates on fuel. ‍ ‍ *Average discount of 42¢ refers to realized average savings per gallon of truck diesel across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner truck stops during H2 2025. The up to discount of $2.00 refers to max realized savings per gallon of truck diesel across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner truck stops during H2 2025. Average discount of 5¢ off per gallon of unleaded is an average across AtoB customer transactions at merchant partner gas stations during H2 2025. AtoB Fuel Card AtoB offers both AtoB Flex and AtoB Unlimited, giving businesses credit and prepaid fleet payment options designed for different operational needs. Beyond helping businesses purchase fuel, the platform combines fleet fuel expense management with spend controls, reporting, and fraud prevention. Key capabilities include: Make vehicle-related purchases anywhere Mastercard is accepted Manage fuel, maintenance, tires, parts, and other approved vehicle expenses from one platform Build business credit through Experian reporting with AtoB Flex Integrate with compatible accounting systems to simplify expense management Access fleet credit card functionality that helps streamline payments and improve cash flow management WEX Fleet Card WEX provides fuel management tools and transaction reporting through participating fuel and maintenance networks. Businesses should evaluate network participation, reporting capabilities, and maintenance coverage when comparing providers. Key capabilities include: Maintenance purchasing through participating networks Fuel management and reporting tools Transaction fees and pricing structures vary by program Check the Wex website for the most up-to-date information regarding product offerings. Coast Fleet Card Coast provides a Visa-based fleet payment platform with mobile authorization and expense management tools for businesses managing vehicle-related spending. Key capabilities include: Vehicle-related purchases beyond fuel Mobile authorization for driver transactions Reporting and expense management tools that help track maintenance and operating costs Check the Coast website for the most up-to-date information regarding product offerings. When comparing fuel card providers, consider maintenance coverage, truck stop discounts, reporting capabilities, and spend controls, not just rebates on fuel. The right fuel card should help reduce administrative work while improving visibility into maintenance and fuel expenses across the fleet. Frequently Asked Questions Can I Use a Fleet Fuel Card for Maintenance and Repairs? Yes, but coverage depends on the card network and provider. Fleet cards that allow businesses to make vehicle-related purchases anywhere Mastercard is accepted generally provide broader flexibility at repair shops, parts suppliers, and service centers than closed-network fuel cards. Do Maintenance Purchases Count Toward Fuel Card Rebate Tiers? This varies by provider. Some fleet card programs calculate rebates based on fuel volume only, while others may consider total spending. Businesses should review program terms before applying. What Is the Best Fleet Fuel Card for Small Businesses That Need Maintenance Coverage? The best fuel card for small business operations combines maintenance coverage, spend controls, reporting, fraud prevention, and fleet expense management. Businesses should also evaluate network acceptance, transaction fees, and maintenance purchasing capabilities based on how their fleet operates. AtoB offers both credit and prepaid fleet payment options designed for different operational needs. How Does Fleet Card Data Help with Preventive Maintenance? Fleet cards capture odometer readings at fuel transactions, which can trigger maintenance alerts. Consistent fuel tracking per vehicle over time also flags emerging mechanical issues before they reduce efficiency. Manage Fuel and Maintenance Spend from One Platform with AtoB Managing fuel, maintenance, and driver expenses through separate systems makes it harder to track operating costs across the fleet. A unified fleet financial platform helps businesses consolidate reporting, simplify expense management, and gain greater visibility into vehicle-related spending. AtoB combines fuel savings, fleet expense management, spend controls, fraud prevention, and business credit building within one platform. Whether your fleet operates locally or across multiple job sites, AtoB helps businesses manage fuel and maintenance expenses more efficiently. title: Dianthus Therapeutics Highlights Recent Business Achievements and Reports Q2 2026 Financial Results
summary: Advancing a neuromuscular franchise with claseprubart, a highly potent investigational classical pathway inhibitor, with best-in-disease potential across generalized Myasthenia Gravis (gMG), Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP), and Multifocal Motor Neuropathy (MMN) Phase 3
body_text: Advancing a neuromuscular franchise with claseprubart, a highly potent investigational classical pathway inhibitor, with best-in-disease potential across generalized Myasthenia Gravis (gMG), Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP), and Multifocal Motor Neuropathy (MMN) Phase 3 EMERGE registrational trial of claseprubart in gMG evaluating 300mg/2mL Q2W and 300mg/2mL Q4W initiated in June ‘26, with top-line results anticipated in 2H’28 75% response rate observed in Interim Responder Analysis from first 40 participants completing Part A of Phase 3 CAPTIVATE trial of claseprubart in CIDP, with Part B top-line guidance expected by YE’26 Phase 2 MoMeNtum trial of claseprubart in MMN exceeded its original enrollment target of 36 patients; top-line results with 46 patients on track for December ’26 Building a rheumatology franchise with DNTH212 across our first three prioritized indications of Sjögren’s Disease (SjD), Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), and Dermatomyositis (DM); Phase 1 healthy volunteer data anticipated by YE’26 Advancing DNTH312, an internally developed, first-in-class, next-generation bifunctional fusion protein combining claseprubart and TACI to target potent inhibition of aC1s and BAFF/APRIL for severe autoimmune diseases; DNTH312 aims to be Phase 1 ready by YE’27 Approximately $1.2 billion of cash as of June 30, 2026 provides expected runway into 2030 NEW YORK and WALTHAM, Mass., Aug. 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Dianthus Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: DNTH), a clinical-stage biotechnology company dedicated to developing next-generation therapies to transform the treatment of severe autoimmune diseases, today reported financial results for the second quarter ending June 30, 2026, and provided an update on other recent business achievements. “Our strong execution in the first half of 2026 reflects the continued focus and discipline of the Dianthus team as we advance both claseprubart and DNTH212 for severe autoimmune diseases,” said Marino Garcia, Chief Executive Officer of Dianthus Therapeutics. “With the initiation of our Phase 3 EMERGE registrational trial in gMG, excellent interim results from Part A of our Phase 3 CAPTIVATE trial in CIDP, and completion of enrollment in the Phase 2 MoMeNtum trial in MMN with top-line results expected in December, claseprubart continues to demonstrate its potential as a best-in-disease, pipeline-in-a-product opportunity. In addition, we anticipate Phase 1 healthy volunteer data for DNTH212 by year end. We continue to strengthen our leadership position in autoimmune diseases with today’s announcement of the addition of our innovative, internally developed, first-in-class, next generation, highly potent and half-life extended bifunctional fusion protein, DNTH312.” Claseprubart: Potential Best-in-Disease aC1s Inhibitor for Neuromuscular Diseases Claseprubart is an investigational, clinical-stage, potent monoclonal antibody engineered to selectively target the classical pathway by inhibiting only the active form of the C1s protein, a clinically validated complement target. Claseprubart is designed to enable a more convenient, subcutaneous (S.C.), self-administered injection dosed as infrequently as once every two or four weeks. Claseprubart has the potential to be a best-in-disease pipeline-in-a-product across a range of autoimmune disorders with high unmet need. Generalized Myasthenia Gravis (gMG) Phase 3 EMERGE trial initiated, with top-line results expected in 2H’28: A Phase 3 registrational trial of claseprubart evaluating 300mg/2mL Q2W S.C. and 300mg/2mL Q4W S.C. in gMG patients was initiated in June, with top-line results expected in 2H’28. Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy (CIDP) 75% response rate observed in Interim Responder Analysis from first 40 participants completing Part A of Phase 3 CAPTIVATE trial , exceeding the target response rate of 50% or greater based on precedent set with aC1s inhibition. Results were consistent and clinically meaningful across multiple efficacy measures. Claseprubart was generally well tolerated with no related serious infections, no clinical symptoms of drug-induced lupus (DIL), no related serious adverse events (SAEs) or discontinuations due to safety. Dianthus expects to provide CAPTIVATE Part B top-line guidance by YE’26. Multifocal Motor Neuropathy (MMN) Enrollment completed, exceeding the enrollment target, in the Phase 2 MoMeNtum trial , with top-line results on track for December ‘26: The MoMeNtum trial, a global, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial in patients with MMN, exceeded its original enrollment target of 36 patients. Top-line results with 46 patients are on track for December ’26. All Programs Claseprubart presentations at the American Academy of Neurology (AAN), Peripheral Nerve Society (PNS), and European Academy of Neurology (EAN) meetings described the design of the pivotal Phase 3 CAPTIVATE study in CIDP, Phase 2 MaGic trial results in gMG, Minimal Symptom Expression (MSE) results for claseprubart from MaGic, and potential mechanistic advantages of targeting aC1s in gMG. Presentations are available in the Investors section of the Dianthus website . In March 2026, the Company filed an 8K indicating receipt of written feedback from FDA agreeing to three proposals for all ongoing and planned future claseprubart trials: Removal of anti-nuclear antibodies ("ANAs") as a screening criteria, a common reason for screen failure across all three claseprubart programs; Removal of routine ANA testing during claseprubart clinical trials; and Reclassification of the hypothetical risk of SLE to drug-induced lupus (DIL), a side effect in several classes of widely used medications characterized by the reversal of symptoms upon discontinuation of the precipitating medication. Of note, there have been no cases of either SLE or DIL to date in any claseprubart program. DNTH212: Potential Best-in-Disease, Bifunctional BDCA2 and BAFF/APRIL Inhibitor for Rheumatology Conditions DNTH212 is an investigational, extended half-life bifunctional fusion protein targeting plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) BDCA2 to reduce Type 1 interferon production, while simultaneously inhibiting BAFF/APRIL to suppress B cell function. By targeting both the innate and adaptive immune systems via two clinically validated pathways that are known drivers of autoimmune disease pathogenesis, this complementary and differentiated approach has the potential to address multiple autoimmune indications with improved outcomes. Phase 1 data anticipated by year end: A two-part Phase 1 study in China in healthy volunteers (Part A) and patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (Part B) was initiated in December 2025, with Phase 1 healthy volunteer data anticipated by year end. Upon completion of the Phase 1 study, Dianthus plans to provide an update on next steps for advancing its priority indications in clinical development. Initial indications selected for DNTH212 clinical development: SjD, SLE, and DM were selected as the first three priority indications for DNTH212 clinical development and will serve as the foundation of a synergistic rheumatology franchise for DNTH212. DNTH312: An Internally Developed, First-in-class, Next-generation Bifunctional Fusion Protein Combining Claseprubart and TACI to Target Potent Inhibition of aC1s and BAFF/APRIL for Autoimmune Diseases DNTH312 is an internally developed, investigational, first-in-class, next-generation bifunctional fusion protein combining claseprubart and TACI to target potent inhibition of aC1s and BAFF/APRIL. By targeting two validated pathways with complementary disease modifying mechanisms, DNTH312 expands Dianthus’ leadership position in autoimmune diseases with its potential for best-in-disease efficacy by targeting deeper responses and broader symptom control, while also addressing larger patient populations. DNTH312 demonstrated comparable in vitro potency and aC1s inhibition to claseprubart across several functional assays of Classical Pathway inhibition and a similar depth of IgM, IgA, and IgG reductions vs. published values for povetacicept following a single dose in non-human primates (NHPs). Additionally, DNTH312 is enhanced with YTE half-life extension technology, and has a similar NHP half-life (22 days) to claseprubart, which has an approximately 60-day half-life in humans. DNTH312 aims to be Phase 1 ready by YE’27. Second-Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cash Position – Approximately $1.2 billion of cash, cash equivalents and investments as of June 30, 2026 is projected to provide runway into 2030. R&D Expenses – Research and development (R&D) expenses for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 were $48.7 million, inclusive of $5.6 million of stock-based compensation, compared to $26.3 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, which included $2.5 million of stock-based compensation. This increase in R&D expenses was primarily driven by higher clinical costs and increased headcount to support claseprubart Phase 2 and Phase 3 development. G&A Expenses – General and administrative (G&A) expenses for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 totaled $13.6 million, inclusive of stock-based compensation of $6.3 million, compared to $8.9 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, which included $3.2 million of stock-based compensation. This increase in G&A expenses was primarily due to increased headcount. Net Loss – Net loss for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $50.2 million or $0.90 per share (basic and diluted) compared to $31.6 million or $0.88 per share (basic and diluted) for the quarter ended June 30, 2025. Additional Information – For additional information on the Company’s financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, please refer to the Form 10-Q filed with the SEC. About Claseprubart (DNTH103) Claseprubart is an investigational, clinical-stage, potent monoclonal antibody engineered to selectively target the classical pathway by inhibiting only the active form of the C1s protein, a clinically validated complement target. Claseprubart is enhanced with YTE half-life extension technology designed to enable a more convenient subcutaneous, infrequently dosed, self-administered injection. Additionally, selective inhibition of the classical complement pathway may lower patient risk of infection from encapsulated bacteria by preserving immune activity of the lectin and alternative pathways. As the classical pathway plays a significant role in disease pathology, claseprubart has the potential to be a best-in-disease pipeline-in-a-product across a range of autoimmune disorders with high unmet need. Claseprubart was granted Orphan Drug Designation by the FDA for the treatment of Myasthenia Gravis in May 2026. Dianthus is building a neuromuscular franchise with claseprubart and expects to report top-line data from the Phase 2 MoMeNtum trial in Multifocal Motor Neuropathy in December ’26, to provide an update on timing of top-line data from Part B of the Phase 3 CAPTIVATE trial in Chronic Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyneuropathy by YE’26, and to report top-line results from the Phase 3 EMERGE trial in generalized Myasthenia Gravis in 2H’28. Claseprubart is an investigational agent that is not approved as a therapy in any indication in any jurisdiction worldwide. About DNTH212 DNTH212 is an investigational, extended half-life bifunctional fusion protein targeting plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) BDCA2 to reduce Type 1 interferon production, while simultaneously inhibiting BAFF/APRIL to suppress B cell function. By targeting both the innate and adaptive immune systems via two clinically validated pathways that are known drivers of autoimmune disease pathogenesis, this complementary and differentiated approach has the potential to address multiple autoimmune indications with improved outcomes. Dianthus is building a rheumatology franchise with DNTH212 and has selected Sjögren’s Disease (SjD), Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), and Dermatomyositis (DM) as the first three prioritized indications for clinical development. A two-part Phase 1 study in China in healthy volunteers (Part A) and patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (Part B) is ongoing, with healthy volunteer data expected by YE’26. DNTH212 is an investigational agent that is not approved as a therapy in any indication in any jurisdiction worldwide. About DNTH312 DNTH312 is an internally developed, investigational, first-in-class, next-generation bifunctional fusion protein combining claseprubart and TACI to target potent inhibition of aC1s and BAFF/APRIL. DNTH312 is enhanced with YTE half-life extension technology, similar to claseprubart. By targeting two validated pathways with complementary disease modifying mechanisms, DNTH312 is designed to expand Dianthus’ leadership position in autoimmune diseases with potential for best-in-disease efficacy by targeting deeper responses and broader symptom control, while also addressing larger patient populations. DNTH312 aims to be Phase 1 ready by YE’27. DNTH312 is an investigational agent that is not approved as a therapy in any indication in any jurisdiction worldwide. About Dianthus Therapeutics Dianthus Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company dedicated to developing next-generation therapies to transform the treatment of severe autoimmune diseases. Based in New York City and Waltham, Mass., Dianthus is comprised of an experienced team of biotech and pharma executives who aim to deliver transformative medicines for people living with severe autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. body_text: 2025 Acura MDX Reviews, Pricing & Specs Write a review $51,200 to $75,250 Original MSRP 7.8 of 10 expert review -- avg user rating (0 reviews) Pros Stylish design Comfortable Easy-to-use technology Cons Poor fuel economy No hybrid or plug-in hybrid option Cramped third row 7.8 out of 10 expert review Look & feel 8/10 Technology 9/10 Performance 7/10 Safety 8/10 Form & function 7/10 Cost-effectiveness 8/10 The Acura MDX is the best-selling three-row luxury SUV in history, and the updated 2025 MDX demonstrates why. People want stylish, reliable, and safe vehicles equipped with simple controls, intuitive technology, and enjoyable driving dynamics. Of course, value is a part of that equation, particularly when it comes to fuel economy. We’re happy to report the refreshed 2025 Acura MDX meets nearly all of those requirements. Furthermore, Acura has apparently gotten the user-experience and user-interface message loud and clear, as the changes to the 2025 MDX reflect a shift to simplicity, sophistication, and refinement. Verdict: This year’s updates make the 2025 Acura MDX more appealing than ever. However, this is not a fuel-efficient choice and the standard V6 engine is somewhat underwhelming. Acura needs to install a hybrid or plug-in hybrid in the MDX as soon as possible if it wants to woo customers shopping in this segment. 8/10 Acura makes minor styling modifications to the MDX for the 2025 model year. They include a new grille, revised front bumper, and darkened headlights and taillights. Also, most versions of the SUV get new wheel designs and finishes. The updates are subtle, but they tidy up the front end while giving the sporty and performance versions more visual presence. Interior changes are more impactful. Since a new touchscreen infotainment system debuts in the 2025 MDX, Acura rids the center console of the previous touchpad interface to add more storage. Also, the seats from last year’s MDX Type S model trickle down into the MDX Advance package and MDX A-Spec Advance, while the Type S gets a new seat design for 2025. Acura also quiets the SUV’s cabin with added sound insulation and acoustic laminated window glass. Quality remains an Acura MDX hallmark, though we’d prefer the company eliminate the gloss black plastic trim from the dashboard. It rapidly collects lint, dust, and smudges, and after you wipe it down it remains clean for about five minutes. Thankfully, the MDX provides logically located controls that are easy to find and use. There is a volume knob with a tuning rocker switch on the center console, and Acura places quick-access head-up display and safety feature buttons on the lower left side of the dashboard. That means you need not hunt through the digital instrumentation or infotainment screen searching for them. The updated 2025 Acura MDX lineup adds a new A-Spec Advance trim level that blends maximum luxury with a sportier look. Our test vehicle had this new trim, and with the extra-cost Apex Blue Pearl paint and a $1,350 destination charge, the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) flirted with $70,000 (it was $69,950). If that sounds high for an MDX, you’re correct. But you can spend less on one. In base trim, the MDX starts at $50,900, and that model is nicely equipped. From there, you can add Technology, A-Spec, Advance, and A-Spec Advance equipment. The MDX Type S Advance tops the lineup, offering maximum acceleration and handling in exchange for $74,950, plus the destination charge. 7/10 Acura positions itself as the performance-oriented Asian luxury brand, and backs that up through A-Spec design and Type S engineering—the latter including a turbocharged 3.0-liter V6 engine producing 355 horsepower and 354 lb-ft of torque. However, every Acura is tuned for enjoyable if not outright thrilling driving dynamics, and that’s true of the MDX. Since most MDX buyers choose one with the standard 3.5-liter V6 engine, that’s what we requested for this review. It makes 290 hp at 6,200 rpm and 267 lb-ft of torque at 4,700 running on the recommended premium fuel, delivered to the wheels through a 10-speed automatic transmission equipped with paddle shifters. Acura’s torque-vectoring Super Handling All-Wheel Drive (SH-AWD) system is optional on the MDX base and MDX Technology package, and is standard starting with MDX A-Spec trim. Lower trim levels get front-wheel drive (FWD). The tried-and-true engine supplies good power in this midsize three-row SUV, which weighs north of 4,500 pounds when equipped with SH-AWD. The MDX isn’t slow, but neither is it fast. Comfort, Normal, Sport, Snow, and Individual driving modes are available, and the transmission offers Normal and Sport settings. For the best powertrain response, you’ll want to choose Sport mode and the Sport transmission setting. However, if you employ those on a regular basis, fuel economy will tumble. The A-Spec Advance is EPA-rated at 21 mpg in combined driving, but our test vehicle averaged 18.4 mpg on our Southern California testing loop. We used the Sport/Sport setup only when driving in the mountains. Otherwise, the SUV was in Normal/Normal. You can also tackle twisty mountain roads with confidence. On undulating surfaces, the MDX feels a little soft, and it does allow some roll in corners. But the SUV’s body motions are smooth and consistent instead of sudden and unpredictable, making its behavior easy to trust. We noticed some brake fade while driving the MDX with enthusiasm during a mountain descent on a warm summer day, but otherwise, it proved capable and relatively fun to drive. In typical driving situations, the MDX feels firm and communicative in the city while soaking up speed humps and bumps. Step hard on the accelerator, and swift acceleration gets you into the flow of traffic. Merging onto freeways is not a problem, and the SUV offers a smooth, quiet, and comfortable highway ride. As a commuter or a road tripper, the 2025 Acura MDX is satisfying. Though the MDX is a crossover SUV, it is not made for off-roading. It provides only 7.3 inches of ground clearance unless you choose the MDX Type S Advance, which has an air suspension that increases clearance to 9.4 inches. But with its fancy 21-inch wheels and expensive performance tires, the Type S is not a good choice for off-roading. Acura could build an overlander around that air suspension, but is resisting that trend for now. That’s probably wise, since a lift, all-terrain tires, glue-on body kit, and robust roof rack don’t align with the automaker’s performance-oriented identity. 7/10 This year, the MDX Advance and MDX A-Spec Advance get 16-way power-adjustable front seats with heating, ventilation, and eight different massage programs. They’re wrapped in perforated, piped, and quilted leather, and are exceptionally comfortable and supportive. Previously, these seats were reserved for the MDX Type S. You can configure the second row as a three-person bench seat or individual bucket seats. When it isn’t in use, the middle section of the backrest folds down to offer cupholders and a storage tray, or to allow long items to fit into the SUV. Alternatively, you can remove and store the center section to create individual second-row seats and create a large pass-through to the third row. The MDX’s outboard second-row seating positions are comfortable with plenty of leg room and thigh support, and side window shades cover nearly all of the window glass in all but the base MDX. A triple-zone automatic climate control system is standard on every version of the SUV. The third-row seat is hard for adults to enter and exit, and is uncomfortable for grown-ups. The seat is low and lacks leg support, and there isn’t much room for feet under the second-row seats. Reserve this area for younger children. In-cabin storage space is adequate. The new center console adds a handy tray next to the cupholders, and the wireless smartphone charging pad is easy to access. Under the center armrest is a small cube-shaped area, and the glove compartment is nearly full when the owner’s manual and other vehicle documentation is kept there. That leaves small trays in the armrests and the lower door panel pockets to accommodate loose items. Cargo volume measures 16.3 cubic feet behind the third-row seat. That’s enough for groceries, backpacks, or a few duffel bags. Acura provides a sizable well on the left side of the cargo area, and a large compartment under the load floor offers hidden storage. Folding and raising the 50/50-split third-row seats is a manual operation, which we prefer. Waiting for seats to power down or up is a drag, and we dislike the idea of repairing them one day. With the third row folded flat, the MDX provides 39.1 cubic feet of cargo space. Drop the second row, and this SUV can carry up to 71.4 cubic feet of cargo. 9/10 Arguably, the 2025 MDX’s new infotainment system is the game changer for this SUV. It has a 12.3-inch touchscreen display, Alexa Built-in, and Google Built-in, the latter with complimentary access to Google Maps, Google Assistant, and Google Play for three years. This system eliminates the MDX’s old True Touchpad Interface (TTI) setup. The theory behind the TTI was well intended, but it required a distracting amount of hand-eye coordination to use while driving. The change is a good one. The new system and its digital voice assistants work like the smartphone that is ever-present in your life, bringing a natural and intuitive interface to the MDX’s dashboard. However, if you’re a SiriusXM satellite radio fan, be advised that you’ll do without it unless you have the app on your phone and stream it through the Bluetooth connection or the wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto connectivity. In addition, the latest version of AcuraLink connected services is standard, and the infotainment system supports an AT&T 4G LTE Wi-Fi hotspot. Acura has also upgraded the base MDX model’s premium sound system to 11 speakers, and starting with the MDX Technology the SUV features Bang & Olufsen audio systems with 19 or 31 speakers. Only the MDX Type S Advance gets the high-end 31-speaker setup. During our evaluation, we found the new infotainment and Bang & Olufsen sound systems nearly flawless. Google Assistant responded quickly and accurately to queries and commands, though it does not allow voice control of the climate system. We effortlessly paired an iPhone 15 to the Bluetooth connection, easily streamed Apple Music and Pandora, and switched between CarPlay and the native Google environment without trouble. The new infotainment system pairs with a 12.3-inch digital instrumentation display. Two themes are available, each with a graphic representation of the MDX in the middle that shows exterior lighting and safety system status. The display is simple, but that makes it easy to use and reference. Our test vehicle also had a 10.5-inch head-up display showing a comprehensive amount of data on the windshield within the driver’s line of sight. All that’s missing from the display are blind-spot monitoring alerts to show when other vehicles are nearby the SUV. In addition, the MDX Advance and MDX A-Spec Advance feature a surround-view camera system offering front, side, and rear views. When parking, you can quickly activate the front and side cameras using a button on the end of the windshield wiper stalk, making them quickly accessible. 8/10 The 2025 MDX benefits from hardware upgrades that make its AcuraWatch collection of driver assistance features operate with improved accuracy and refinement. An expanded version called AcuraWatch 360 also debuts for 2025 as an exclusive feature on the MDX Type S Advance. All MDX models have forward-collision warning, automatic emergency braking, lane-departure warning, lane-keeping assist, lane-centering assist, blind-spot monitoring, and rear cross-traffic alert. Adaptive cruise control is also standard, as well as Traffic Jam Assist, a semi-autonomous driving assistance system for use in heavy traffic. Starting with the MDX Technology, the SUV has front and rear parking sensors and a low-speed automatic braking system. AcuraWatch 360 is new for 2025. It employs additional front corner radar units, a new front millimeter wave radar unit, and an upgraded front camera. Those components make it possible for Acura to offer front cross-traffic alert, evasive steering warning, and an active lane-change assist function that can help prevent collisions. This package also adds a cornering speed assist system, but in our experience, these are typically too aggressive when it comes to speed reduction. AcuraWatch 360 is available only on the Type S Advance in 2025. During testing, the standard AcuraWatch features performed well. We noted one false lane-departure notification and the tech could not navigate a tricky T-shaped intersection on a rural two-lane road. Otherwise, it behaved with remarkable accuracy and refinement. You’re aware of the subtle steering and braking inputs, but they don’t cause irritation. However, we did not like driving the MDX with the adaptive cruise control off and the lane-centering function on. In that use case, the tech does feel unnatural and unwanted. Also, we’re still not fans of Acura’s lane-departure warning notification, which wobbles rather than vibrates the steering wheel. Since the 2025 MDX is structurally identical to the 2024 model, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has carried over the SUV’s five-star overall rating. However, since versions with SH-AWD don’t have a rollover resistance rating, the NHTSA does not offer a final judgment on those models. As of this writing, the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) has no comment regarding 2025 MDX crash tests. The 2024 MDX earned the highest Top Safety Pick+ rating. 8/10 The 2025 Acura MDX counts numerous midsize luxury SUVs as its rivals, but it occupies a sweet spot in the segment where it boasts one of the lowest prices combined with attractive design, a quality interior, and appealing technology. That might be why Acura has dialed back its complimentary maintenance plan to cover only the first scheduled visit during the first year or 12,000 miles of driving. Previously, it was two years or 24,000 miles. The Audi Q7, BMW X5, Genesis GV80, Lexus TX, Mercedes-Benz GLE, and Volvo XC90 all cost more than the MDX. Of that sextet, only the Audi, Lexus, and Volvo include a third-row seat as standard equipment. However, mild hybrid, hybrid, and plug-in hybrid powertrains are common in these MDX alternatives, except for the Genesis. They can surpass the Acura in performance, efficiency, or both at the same time. Cadillac and Infiniti also offer competitors to the Acura, but neither is preferable to the MDX. You might also consider the surprisingly powerful and sophisticated Lincoln Aviator, but it’s a comparatively pricey SUV. Likewise, the Land Rover Defender 110 and Land Rover Discovery cost more, but they offer the off-roading capability missing from the MDX. If you have no need to wade across streams or clamber over rocks, the 2025 Acura MDX presents a strong case for cost-effectiveness without compromise. The only exception relates to fuel economy. This is not an efficient SUV, and Acura doesn’t offer the electrified powertrains available in many of the MDX’s rivals. Published Jul 9, 2024 by Christian Wardlaw Christian Wardlaw has 25 years of experience reviewing cars and has served in editorial leadership roles with Edmunds, J.D. Power, the New York Daily News, Autobytel, and Vehix. Chris prefers to focus on the cars people actually buy rather than the cars about which people dream, and emphasizes the importance of fuel economy and safety as much as how much fun a car is to drive. Chris is married to an automotive journalist, is the father of four daughters, and lives in Southern California. User reviews for 2025 Acura MDX Write a review There are no reviews on this car. title: La red que no se detiene: así reparten a México los productos ultraprocesados
summary: México produce y distribuye más ultraprocesados que cualquier país de LATAM. Descubre cómo la logística los lleva a cada rincón.
body_text: Sign in Welcome! Log into your account Forgot your password? Get help Password recovery Recover your password A password will be e-mailed to you. La red que no se detiene: así reparten a México los productos ultraprocesados Camiones que no paran, tiendas en cada esquina y un país que compra 212 kilos de comida industrializada por persona al año: el motor logístico que convirtió a México en el mayor productor y distribuidor de ultraprocesados de América Latina, y en el cuarto consumidor del mundo. Conocimiento Industria 05/08/2026 Antes de llegar a la mesa, una bolsa de botanas o un refresco recorre un camino más largo de lo que parece: fábricas, centros de distribución, bodegas regionales y decenas de miles de changarros y tiendas de conveniencia repartidos por todo el territorio nacional. Esa cadena, engrasada durante décadas por la industria alimentaria, explica en buena medida por qué México ocupa el primer lugar en producción y distribución de productos ultraprocesados en América Latina, de acuerdo con el Laboratorio de Datos contra la Obesidad (LabDO). ¿Qué son los productos ultraprocesados? Se trata de formulaciones industriales hechas a partir de ingredientes refinados, aditivos, colorantes, saborizantes artificiales y conservadores, con escasa o nula presencia de alimentos frescos. Su sello distintivo es que están diseñados para durar meses en anaquel, consumirse de inmediato y resultar altamente palatables gracias a combinaciones de azúcar, sal y grasa. Botanas saladas, refrescos, galletas, pan de caja, embutidos y sopas instantáneas forman parte de este grupo, pensado desde su origen para viajar largas distancias sin perder frescura ni sabor. El origen de los alimentos procesados La industrialización de la comida no nació con el objetivo de enfermar a nadie, sino de resolver un problema logístico: cómo alimentar ciudades cada vez más grandes y alejadas del campo. Las técnicas de enlatado, deshidratación y pasteurización, perfeccionadas durante los conflictos bélicos del siglo XX, permitieron conservar alimentos por meses y abrieron paso a un comercio de alcance nacional e internacional. Con la posguerra llegaron los aditivos sintéticos y el empaque plástico, y con ellos, productos capaces de sobrevivir semanas en un tráiler o en una bodega sin refrigeración. América Latina, y México en particular, se sumó a esa ola desde los años setenta, cuando las corporaciones transnacionales de alimentos y bebidas expandieron sus plantas y rutas de distribución hacia el país, aprovechando su ubicación estratégica y su cercanía con Estados Unidos. La logística que domina los anaqueles Lo que distingue a México no es solo cuánto produce, sino la eficacia con la que coloca esos productos en cualquier rincón del país. La industria de ultraprocesados construyó, durante décadas, una infraestructura de distribución capilar: centros logísticos regionales que abastecen a distribuidores locales, y estos a su vez surten a cientos de miles de tiendas de abarrotes, misceláneas y puestos callejeros, muchos en zonas rurales sin otro punto de venta de alimentos cerca. Esa red informal, con rutas de reparto frecuentes y flexibles, logra algo que la agricultura fresca no siempre consigue: un refresco o una bolsa de frituras llega, sin cadena de frío y sin perder calidad, a comunidades que rara vez reciben un cargamento de verduras. Ese modelo explica en buena medida por qué el acceso a frutas, verduras y proteínas frescas sigue limitado, en especial entre los sectores de menores ingresos, según señaló la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO) al ser consultada por LabDO. Los alimentos frescos exigen refrigeración, tiempos de venta cortos y rutas costosas; los ultraprocesados se mueven con una logística barata, estandarizada y escalable, que multiplica sus puntos de venta. A esa ecuación se suma el ritmo de vida urbano: el tráfico, las largas jornadas laborales y el estrés dejan poco tiempo para cocinar, y comer fuera de casa se volvió habitual para millones de personas. Esa demanda de rapidez encontró en la industria de ultraprocesados a un proveedor perfecto, capaz de surtir tiendas de conveniencia, puestos de comida rápida y aplicaciones de entrega con opciones hipercalóricas, baratas y disponibles a cualquier hora. Tacos, hamburguesas y pizzas encabezan las preferencias de comida rápida, mientras que botanas saladas, bebidas azucaradas, dulces y sopas instantáneas dominan las compras para el hogar. El resultado se refleja en las cifras de consumo: la compra per cápita de estos productos en México alcanza los 212 kilogramos al año , de acuerdo con datos de la Organización Panamericana de la Salud (OPS), y más del 70 por ciento de la población los consume de manera habitual, según la FAO. Esa penetración no sería posible sin la maquinaria de distribución que lleva estos productos hasta el último rincón del país, muchas veces con mayor eficiencia que los propios sistemas de abasto de alimentos frescos. Un costo que se mide en salud La otra cara de esta eficiencia logística es un problema de salud pública que crece a la par de la red de distribución. Más de siete de cada 10 personas adultas en México tienen exceso de peso, así como 37.3 por ciento de los niños de 5 a 11 años y 7.7 por ciento de los menores de cinco años, lo que equivale a casi 4 millones de infantes, según el Instituto Nacional de Salud Pública (INSP). Entre 2020 y 2023, además, 40.4 por ciento de los adolescentes mexicanos presentaba sobrepeso u obesidad, el grupo con mayor proporción de consumidores habituales de estos productos. El Banco de México, en su Reporte sobre las Economías Regionales de enero-marzo de 2024, ha vinculado el consumo sostenido de ultraprocesados con mayor sobrepeso, obesidad, hipertensión, enfermedades cardiovasculares, diabetes tipo 2, cáncer y riesgo de mortalidad. Frente a ello, especialistas recomiendan limitar la compra de estos productos, leer las etiquetas, priorizar alimentos frescos siempre que sea posible y fomentar la actividad física entre niños y adolescentes, el grupo más expuesto a una cadena de distribución que, hasta ahora, ha sido más eficiente vendiendo comida industrializada que fruta fresca. Relacionado Maria Saucedo María es una periodista experimentada que combina su formación en letras con una visión estratégica de la logística, creando contenido inspirador e informativo para nuestro blog. title: L3Harris Achieves Historic First Flight Success with Perimeter Truss Reflector Technology
summary: L3Harris Technologies successfully deployed its perimeter truss reflector onboard the ViaSat-3 Flight 3 satellite, marking the first flight for the L3Harris’ perimeter truss reflector design.
body_text: L3Harris Technologies successfully deployed its perimeter truss reflector onboard the ViaSat-3 Flight 3 satellite, marking the first flight for the company's perimeter truss reflector design. The reflector will support high-speed broadband connectivity across the Asia-Pacific region. The successful deployment represents a significant milestone for L3Harris' perimeter truss antenna technology. The reflector achieved first-flight success following the satellite's launch from Kennedy Space Center in Florida aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on April 29, 2026. "L3Harris delivers innovative antenna technology to Viasat to extend secure, reliable connectivity to customers across the Asia-Pacific region," said Wes Langston, Vice President and General Manager, Surveillance Systems, L3Harris. "This reflector is 30% more compact than the industry standard perimeter truss reflectors while maintaining exceptional surface precision, focusing signals with near-perfect accuracy to maximize data capacity and deliver superior broadband performance to users." L3Harris is a supplier of large deployable mesh reflector apertures and antenna systems for UHF-Band through Ka-Band. The perimeter truss reflectors feature a reflective mesh surface that maximizes antenna gain and provides improved performance required for advanced communications services. L3Harris builds its perimeter truss antennas, including ViaSat-3 F3’s, in Palm Bay, Florida. L3Harris has delivered more than 130 large deployable reflectors and continues to push the boundaries of space antenna technology. Learn more about L3Harris' Space Antennas Related Capabilities Space Antennas L3Harris makes the difficult seem commonplace with space antennas that push the boundaries of technology and structures that perform reliably in the extreme conditions of space. body_text: View All News GameSquare Expands Premium Gaming IP Portfolio Through Sales Partnership with MEGA 08/03/2026 Agreement adds recognized global gaming properties to GameSquare's growing catalog of IP available to brand partners FRISCO, TX / ACCESS Newswire / August 3, 2026 / GameSquare Holdings, Inc. ("GameSquare" or the "Company") (NASDAQ:GAME), a next-generation media, entertainment, technology and digital native treasury company, today announced a strategic partnership with MEGA Advanced Ltd. ("MEGA"), owner and operator of the Esports Awards and The Mobies, The Mobile Awards. Under the agreement, GameSquare will serve as the sales organization for the Esports Awards and The Mobies. The partnership expands the portfolio of premium gaming and esports intellectual property GameSquare can bring to brands and complements the Company's growing catalog of owned, operated and partner-led properties. GameSquare will leverage its brand relationships and integrated capabilities across creators, content, data, media and live experiences to develop and sell sponsorship opportunities associated with the Esports Awards and The Mobies. "Premium IP is an increasingly important part of GameSquare's strategy and strengthens the value of our end-to-end commercial platform," said Justin Kenna, CEO of GameSquare. "The Esports Awards and The Mobies are recognized platforms that bring together many of the leading players, creators, publishers, organizations and brands across gaming. Adding these properties to our commercial portfolio gives us more high-quality inventory to bring to market and creates another opportunity to connect global brands with highly engaged gaming audiences." Founded in 2016, the Esports Awards recognizes the players, teams, creators, publishers, brands and innovators shaping the global competitive-gaming industry. The Mobies was subsequently established as a dedicated awards platform celebrating excellence and innovation throughout mobile gaming. "We have built the Esports Awards and The Mobies into global platforms that celebrate the people and companies advancing gaming and mobile culture," said Mike Ashford, CEO of MEGA. "GameSquare brings extensive brand relationships and an integrated set of commercial capabilities across gaming, creators, content and experiences. We believe this partnership can expand the commercial reach of both properties and create compelling new ways for brands to participate in our events and communities." The agreement builds upon GameSquare's strategy of combining premium gaming and entertainment IP with a scaled commercial infrastructure designed to help brands reach Gen Z, Gen Alpha and Millennial audiences. By expanding the number of properties available through its platform, GameSquare can create additional sponsorship inventory, develop larger integrated brand programs and extend successful partnerships across multiple areas of its ecosystem. About MEGA MEGA is a global gaming and esports media company dedicated to uniting gaming globally through world-class events, creative services, and commercial partnerships. The company owns and operates industry-leading award show properties including the Esports Awards and The Mobies, alongside Tempo, its full-service creative, production, and commercial agency. With expertise spanning live events, broadcast production, content creation, social media, esports operations, and brand partnerships, MEGA works with publishers, teams, creators, and global brands to deliver impactful experiences for gaming audiences worldwide. For more information, visit: https://www.megaadvanced.com/ About GameSquare Holdings, Inc. GameSquare (NASDAQ:GAME) is a cutting-edge media, entertainment, and technology company transforming how brands and publishers connect with Gen Z, Gen Alpha, and Millennial audiences. With a platform that spans award-winning creative services, advanced analytics, and FaZe Esports, one of the most iconic gaming organizations, we operate one of the largest gaming media networks in North America. As a digital-native business, GameSquare provides brands with unparalleled access to world-class creators and talent, delivering authentic connections across gaming, esports, and youth culture. Complementing our operating strategy, GameSquare has developed an innovative treasury management program designed to generate yield and enhance capital efficiency, reinforcing our commitment to building a dynamic, high-performing media company at the intersection of culture, technology, and next-generation financial innovation. To learn more, visit www.gamesquare.com . title: AAR showcases safety culture and expanded engineering capabilities during FAA visit
summary: Wood Dale, Illinois — AAR CORP., the leading parts, repair, and software platform in the aviation aftermarket, hosted Jackie Black, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Division Manager for Aircraft Maintenance, for visits to the Company’s Engineering Services and Airframe Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) operations in Greensboro, North Carolina last week.
body_text: AAR welcomed Jackie Black (fifth from left), Federal Aviation Administration Division Manager for Aircraft Maintenance, to its Engineering Services and Airframe MRO facilities in Greensboro, North Carolina, on August 4, 2026. Wood Dale, Illinois — AAR CORP., the leading parts, repair, and software platform in the aviation aftermarket, hosted Jackie Black, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Division Manager for Aircraft Maintenance, for visits to the Company’s Engineering Services and Airframe Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (MRO) operations in Greensboro, North Carolina, last week. Mr. Black’s visit began with a tour of AAR’s Engineering Services facility in Greensboro. The operation joined AAR’s Engineering Services network following the acquisition of Aircraft Reconfig Technologies (ART) earlier this year. The ART acquisition expanded AAR’s engineering capabilities and included an Organization Designation Authorization (ODA), which authorizes qualified organizations to perform certain certification activities on behalf of the FAA and further strengthens AAR’s ability to support customers with specialized engineering and regulatory expertise. The visit provided an opportunity for AAR’s Engineering Services team to showcase its capabilities and discuss how the acquisition enhances AAR’s engineering expertise, certification capabilities, and customer support offerings. Mr. Black then visited AAR’s Airframe MRO facility in Greensboro, where he led a site-wide safety stand down. A common practice across the aviation industry, safety stand downs provide dedicated time for team members to step away from daily operations, discuss safety priorities, share best practices, and reinforce the culture that helps keep team members and the flying public safe. The session focused on the FAA’s priorities and the shared commitment between industry and regulators to maintaining the highest standards of aviation safety. He then participated in a roundtable discussion with AAR inspectors, auditors, and operational leaders. Topics included regulatory oversight, certification processes, and the coordination enabled through AAR’s Certificate Management Unit (CMU), which oversees multiple FAA-certificated locations. As one of two independent MROs operating under a CMU structure, AAR shared insights on maintaining consistency, compliance, and safety across its network while reinforcing the strong working relationship between the Company and the FAA. “We appreciated the opportunity for our team members to connect directly with FAA leadership and discuss the shared responsibility we all have in advancing aviation safety,” said Art Smith, AAR’s Vice President and Chief Quality Officer. “These conversations strengthen collaboration, encourage the exchange of ideas, and reinforce the culture of safety, quality, and compliance that guides our work every day.” For more information on AAR’s safety culture, visit https://www.aarcorp.com/en/about/safety-and-certifications/ . About AAR AAR is a leading global aerospace and defense aftermarket solutions company with operations in over 20 countries. Headquartered in the Chicago area, AAR supports commercial and government customers through three primary operating segments: Parts Supply; Repair, Engineering, and Software; and Government Solutions. Additional information can be found at aarcorp.com .
