No obligation — just a concrete plan.

title: Kodiak Sciences Announces First Patients Enrolled in Global Phase 3 ALTO trial of KSI-501 in Patients with Diabetic Macular Edema
summary: Phase 3 ALTO trial designed to demonstrate superiority of KSI-501 versus aflibercept in patients with diabetic macular edema PALO ALTO, Calif., Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kodiak Sciences Inc. (Nasdaq: KOD), a precommercial retina-focused biotechnology company committed to researching, developing
body_text: Phase 3 ALTO trial designed to demonstrate superiority of KSI-501 versus aflibercept in patients with diabetic macular edema PALO ALTO, Calif. , Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kodiak Sciences Inc. (Nasdaq: KOD), a precommercial retina-focused biotechnology company committed to researching, developing and commercializing transformative therapeutics, today announced that the first patients have been enrolled in the global Phase 3 ALTO trial evaluating KSI-501 in patients with diabetic macular edema (DME). KSI-501 is an investigational, first-in-class bispecific therapy built on Kodiak's ABC® Platform and designed to potently inhibit two complementary pathways implicated in retinal vascular disease: interleukin (IL)-6-mediated inflammation and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-mediated vascular permeability and neovascularization. The ALTO trial is designed to demonstrate the superiority of bispecific (anti-VEGF, anti-IL-6) KSI-501 versus monospecific (anti-VEGF) aflibercept in patients with DME. ALTO is the second registrational Phase 3 trial of KSI-501, following the DAYBREAK study in patients with wet AMD. ALTO explores whether dual inhibition of immune and vascular pathways can deliver deeper and more sustained disease control for patients with DME and evaluates two dosing regimens, one regimen with intensive dosing and a second regimen with individualized dosing intervals of up to every six months. "Initiating ALTO is an important next step for KSI-501 and for our broader effort to advance multifunctional retinal medicines that address disease biology beyond VEGF alone," said Victor Perlroth, M.D., Chief Executive Officer of Kodiak. "Anti-VEGF therapies have transformed the treatment of DME, yet many patients continue to live with persistent retinal fluid, incomplete visual recovery and the burden of frequent ongoing injections. We believe that inhibiting the immune-focused IL-6 pathway alongside the vessel-focused VEGF pathway, further enhanced with the durability of our ABC Platform, may achieve deeper and more sustained control of this disease." "It has long been believed that there is more to be gained for patients with DME by targeting mechanisms beyond VEGF, and in particular by addressing the chronic, low-grade inflammatory state that often persists in patients who have suboptimal response to anti-VEGF monotherapy," said Margaret Chang, M.D., M.S., Co-Director of Clinical Research at Retina Consultants Medical Group. "Recent results from the Phase 2 ALLUVIUM study demonstrated that IL-6 inhibition alone can lead to clinically meaningful functional and anatomic benefits in DME patients, providing evidence that the IL-6 pathway is biologically active in diabetic eye diseases and operates independently of VEGF-driven pathology. Importantly, the recent Phase 2 BARDENAS study further suggested that dual inhibition of VEGF and IL-6 may offer synergistic effects, with the potential to deliver superior vision gains and improved fluid control versus targeting either pathway alone." "DME is a multifactorial disease in which vascular leakage, blood-retinal barrier dysfunction and immune signaling together drive retinal edema and vision loss," said J. Pablo Velazquez-Martin, M.D., Chief Medical Officer of Kodiak. "Our ALTO study is designed to rigorously evaluate whether dual inhibition of IL-6 and VEGF translates into meaningful benefit for patients, including the potential for better vision gains and greater fluid control, and through Kodiak's ABC biopolymer conjugate platform the potential for superior durability. Alongside the primary visual acuity endpoint, the study is powered for a key secondary endpoint of two-step or greater improvement on the Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Scale (DRSS), and it evaluates a regimen with dosing intervals extending to six months. Our objective is to characterize efficacy, anatomic response and durability in a single Phase 3 program." About the ALTO Study The ALTO Study (KSMP002-S1) is a global, multicenter, randomized, double-masked, active comparator-controlled Phase 3 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of intravitreal KSI-501 5 mg compared with intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg in patients with visual impairment secondary to center-involved DME. Approximately 910 patients, treatment-naïve or previously treated, will be randomized 5:3:5 to one of three arms: Arm A: KSI-501 5 mg every 8 weeks, with monthly assessment for additional individualized dosing, following six monthly loading doses Arm B: KSI-501 5 mg on an individualized regimen of every 4 to 24 weeks, following six monthly loading doses Arm C: aflibercept 2 mg every 8 weeks, following five monthly loading doses The primary endpoint is the mean change in best-corrected visual acuity from baseline to the average of Week 48 and Week 52. The key secondary endpoint is the proportion of patients improving two or more steps on the DRSS from baseline at Week 48. Additional secondary and exploratory endpoints evaluate visual function, retinal anatomy, treatment burden and durability, and safety. Participants will be treated and followed for approximately 96 weeks. Additional information about ALTO, also known as Study KSMP002-S1, is available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07734844 . The Potential of Dual IL-6 and VEGF Inhibition in DME VEGF is an established driver of vascular permeability and abnormal vessel growth in retinal vascular disease, and anti-VEGF therapy has revolutionized the treatment of DME by reducing retinal fluid and delivering meaningful vision gains for the majority of patients. Yet significant room for improvement remains. Across pivotal DME trials, a substantial proportion of patients have persistent edema despite ongoing treatment, and most patients do not achieve 20/20 vision. While recent intravitreal biologics have extended dosing intervals, many patients still require frequent injections to sustain their best possible visual outcome. IL-6 is a pro-inflammatory cytokine and immune growth factor implicated in inflammatory signaling, endothelial dysfunction and disruption of the blood-retinal barrier. Ocular IL-6 is elevated in patients with DME, and higher intraocular IL-6 levels have been associated with poorer visual outcomes in patients treated with anti-VEGF monotherapy. KSI-501 is designed to address these complementary mechanisms in a single intravitreal medicine. The VEGF-trap component mimics the native VEGF receptors and is designed to inhibit VEGF-mediated vascular permeability and neovascularization. The anti-IL-6 antibody component is designed to inhibit IL-6-mediated inflammatory signaling and normalize the blood-retinal barrier. The ABC Platform-based design, with its signature 20-day intraocular half-life, is intended to support sustained intraocular activity and extended durability. In preclinical models, KSI-501 was shown to be a potent inhibitor of both VEGF and IL-6 and to normalize the blood-retinal barrier, opening the possibility that KSI-501 may be a disease-modifying therapy for retinal vascular diseases. About KSI-501 KSI-501 is an investigational anti-IL-6, VEGF-trap bispecific therapy built on the ABC platform and is being developed for high prevalence retinal vascular diseases to address the leading unmet needs of extended durability and targeting disease biology beyond VEGF for differentiated efficacy. KSI-501 is designed to provide high immediacy/efficacy, driven by the enhanced formulation, and high durability, driven by the ABC platform and our science of durability. Kodiak has advanced KSI-501 into the registrational Phase 3 study DAYBREAK to evaluate its efficacy and safety in wet AMD. DAYBREAK uses KSI-501's enhanced 50 mg/mL formulation containing both conjugated and unconjugated antibody that is intended to balance immediacy and durability. DAYBREAK has completed enrollment. Topline data for the one-year primary endpoint in DAYBREAK are expected in September 2026. Kodiak has also advanced KSI-501 into the registrational Phase 3 ALTO study designed to demonstrate the superiority of bispecific KSI-501 (anti-VEGF, anti-IL-6) versus monospecific aflibercept (anti-VEGF) in patients with diabetic macular edema. The ALTO study is now enrolling patients. About Kodiak Sciences Inc. Kodiak Sciences (Nasdaq: KOD) is a pre-commercial retina-focused biotechnology company committed to researching, developing and commercializing transformative therapeutics. We are focused on bringing new science to the design and manufacture of next-generation retinal medicines to prevent and treat the leading causes of blindness globally. We are developing a portfolio of three late-stage clinical programs. Zenkuda™ (tarcocimab tedromer) has a BLA-ready profile in diabetic retinopathy, retinal vein occlusion and wet AMD, and, together with KSI-501, is being explored in the BLA-facing Phase 3 DAYBREAK wet AMD study, with topline data expected in September 2026. Zenkuda and KSI-501 target the $15 billion anti-VEGF market across retinal vascular diseases. KSI-101 is a bispecific protein being explored in two BLA-facing Phase 3 studies in Macular Edema Secondary to Inflammation (MESI). Topline data for Pivotal Analysis 1 (PEAK) are expected in December 2026 and Pivotal Analysis 2 (PEAK+PINNACLE) in 2Q 2027. title: Types of daily suggested workouts for runners
summary: Garmin daily suggested workouts are a great way to prepare for an upcoming training cycle — or recalibrate and recover.
body_text: Fitness Types of daily suggested workouts for runners August 5, 2026 Runners are always in pursuit of their personal best, and Garmin daily suggested workouts are a great way to prepare for an upcoming training cycle — or recalibrate and recover after you’ve given it your all. This feature aims to improve fitness levels while building a foundation for future performances. At its core, the daily suggested workouts feature helps runners by using one’s data to understand how different workout structures can stimulate and develop specific aspects of performance. So, no matter if you’re an entry-level runner with Forerunner® 70 or an elite runner with Forerunner 970 , you’ll get workouts built specifically for you. How does it work? Daily suggested workouts take performance data, such as intensity level and impact of efforts, as well as your current fitness level, training history and recovery state to create the best workout routine for you. You can expect evenly paced runs at various intensities and durations to be mixed with interval-type workouts. What’s right for you today is determined by what you’ve been doing lately. Been taking some time off? Expect to find yourself working to build your endurance base first. When you maintain your routine, you’ll discover a built-in schedule of daily suggested workouts. This means harder training weeks are mixed with more modest ones to avoid stagnation and help you shatter performance plateaus. Training fundamentals Training means regularly challenging yourself with the goal of improving performance over time. It’s a process of sparking physiological adaptation. Tackling varied challenges is the key to constructing a solid foundation for your performance, forging strengths and minimizing weaknesses along the way. You can’t push yourself to the max in every direction every day and expect long-term results. Successful athletes typically concentrate on improving a single aspect of performance at a time. In the weight room, you can focus on leg strength one day and upper body strength the next. Strive to apply the same principle when you lace up your running shoes by focusing on different efforts when you hit the road. As you discover the training run structures suggested by this program, keep in mind that categorization of workouts is based on the primary benefit of your development. Below the surface, however, your physiology works across a continuum to support performance. That means, for example, that a run designed to build your anaerobic capacity can still have a significant aerobic element to it. Training Load Focus screen What types of runs can you expect? There are seven workout structures that can be recommended based on your situation. There will be days when the best option is for you to rest up for your next challenge. The duration of an endurance-building run will be longer or shorter based on what you can handle today. If you’re already familiar with the Training Load Focus screen in the Training Status widget, you will probably notice that these runs map neatly onto the Anaerobic, Low Aerobic and High Aerobic bars that help guide your Training Load toward the right balance. Low-intensity aerobic training runs Active “recovery” runs Although recovery runs are slow and easy, performing an active recovery workout correctly and gaining the intended benefit requires great discipline. It’s easy to let your intensity and speed drift upward without proper focus and intent. Metabolic byproducts accumulate in your muscles during harder, more intense workouts. The goal of recovery runs is to gently increase circulation, flushing cellular waste out of your muscles in the process. Overdo it and push the limits during your recovery run and you will miss out on the rewards and add stress to your body. Plus, entry-level runners can work in other recovery workouts, such as walks, with a Forerunner 70 or Forerunner 170 smartwatch. This is designed to give runners the same benefits as active recovery without the additional impact of running. Endurance “base” runs Endurance-focused runs will likely represent the bulk of your low-intensity training. And like recovery runs, part of the challenge comes from keeping the intensity of your efforts low to help build your aerobic stamina. This is particularly true if your route of choice includes uphill segments where intensity can drift upward quickly. The best duration for your own endurance-based runs depends on your current fitness level and will typically vary runner to runner. Experienced runners might partake in a long run where the focus is maintaining a steady pace, whereas an entry-level runner with Forerunner 70 or Forerunner 170 might be prompted to complete a run/walk workout. Keeping an eye on your heart rate is the perfect way to control intensity during your run. The heart rate (HR) zone you work to maintain during your endurance-building runs should be adjusted to match your personal parameters. This is typically below 80% of your maximum heart rate, so it’s worth checking to make sure your HR max is set correctly for you. Key benefits of these slow runs include building stronger muscles and improved running efficiency across the board. This includes your cardiorespiratory system, muscle function, metabolism and running form. Endurance runs also teach your body to burn fat better. Enjoy getting an enormous number of strides under your belt without the strain that accumulates rapidly during higher-intensity efforts. High-intensity aerobic training runs Tempo Today’s Suggestion Tempo screen Tempo runs are where things start to pick up speed. You need to put in some effort to keep up the pace but can keep going for a while if you want to go for it. Performed at your so-called marathon pace, the target intensity for your tempo runs is sandwiched in between your endurance runs and threshold runs. These runs can be suggested as steady-pace workouts or they can take the form of relatively gentle interval runs, where the harder segments are longer and performed with an intensity well below an all-out sprint. Tempo runs are a terrific way to build general fitness and contribute nicely to the high-intensity aerobic bar on your Training Load Focus screen in the Training Status widget. Threshold While VO2 max defines your maximum aerobic performance capacity, your lactate threshold relates to how long you can sustain higher intensity levels relative to your maximum capacity. When the intensity of your performance exceeds your lactate threshold, fatigue accumulates quickly. Practically speaking, your lactate threshold translates into the pace or intensity that you can sustain for about 40 minutes to an hour. If two runners have the same VO2 max but one has a higher lactate threshold, you can expect the runner with the higher lactate threshold to win a 10K race. The runner with the higher lactate threshold should be able sustain an intensity closer to their VO2 max for a longer time. The goal of threshold runs is to increase your lactate threshold. To do that, you will need to run at or slightly above your lactate threshold pace or intensity level for an extended period. This results in a hard day’s run, so make sure you’re up for the challenge. “VO2 max” or aerobic capacity VO2 max-improving training runs are typically built around longer high-intensity intervals punctuated with lighter efforts that give you a chance to recover before ramping up the intensity again. Ideally you will maintain the higher intensity level long enough for your aerobic system to catch up to the energy demand of your performance and continue for a handful of minutes. Punctuating these longer high-intensity intervals with a chance to catch your breath ultimately allows you to run more total minutes at this level, amplifying the signal to your body that it’s time to adapt to the challenge. The intensity of these efforts is above your lactate threshold, which means you will only be able to sustain them for a relatively short time, but the intensity is well below an all-out effort that will leave you quickly exhausted. It may take some trial and error to dial in the right level of intensity for these runs. This awareness comes with time and experience. Anaerobic training runs Anaerobic capacity Equally important to your training are short, vigorous runs designed to boost your anaerobic performance capacity . The high-intensity segments of these runs, however, usually last only 40–60 seconds and are much shorter than in VO2 max training runs. These runs are purposefully structured so that your aerobic energy system is unable to catch up to the energy demand of your performance. This forces your anaerobic energy pathways to carry the burden of synthesizing the molecular fuel (ATP) that powers your muscle contractions. Lactic acid is a byproduct of anaerobic metabolism. It accumulates rapidly in your muscles as you power through these high-intensity interval runs. The accumulation of lactic acid is associated with various aches and often produces a burning sensation in your legs. The cooldown portion of your workout is designed to give your body a head start in clearing lactic acid from your muscles. Anaerobic workouts are not included in daily suggested workouts on the Forerunner 70 or Forerunner 170 smartwatches, but they can be found on advanced and premium Forerunner smartwatches like Forerunner 570 , Forerunner 970 and more. Today’s Suggestion Sprint screen Sprint The final category of training runs included in this system is built around the most explosive efforts you can perform. The extreme nature of these forces means that you can’t sustain them for very long — and that’s the point. This is your opportunity to go all out, leaving it all on the road. Quickly summoning this amount of power from your muscles has a remarkable effect. It improves the ability of your nerves and muscles to work together. This includes developing the sequencing and coordination of muscle contractions and recruiting more muscle fiber units into the movement. These elements translate into your ability to generate higher top speeds. These adaptations fall under the category of neuromuscular power and can have a tremendous impact on your overall performance, especially in racing and general sports performance. Working to increase top speed can also improve your race-pace running economy. Sprint training is most beneficial when you’re well rested and ready to be at your best. This means you shouldn’t expect to see these suggested workouts if you have a significant amount of recovery time remaining due to a hard training session the day before or a bad night’s sleep. Adequate recovery between runs is always important, but it’s especially important here. Pushing your limits while fatigued opens the door to injury. It also means likely missing out on the full developmental benefit of your efforts because your body will struggle to bounce back instead of getting stronger. Now that you’re familiar with the workouts best suited to improve your fitness level and endurance, use Garmin Run Coach in the Garmin Connect™ app to develop a training plan that will get you across the finish line. Plus, don’t forget to strap on one of our latest running smartwatches .

title: How Can a Global Payouts API Scale GOTV Campaigns?
summary: Need to scale civic campaigns? Discover how a payouts API automates micro-influencer compensation to streamline compliance and voter engagement.
body_text: Scaling modern voter engagement initiatives requires moving past outdated outreach strategies and embracing peer-to-peer mobilization. When advocacy groups deploy massive networks of student and micro-influencers to drive civic participation, finance departments quickly encounter severe operational bottlenecks. Implementing a unified payout system bridges the gap between grassroots momentum and secure, automated corporate compliance. Non-profits and advocacy platforms scaling Get Out the Vote (GOTV) initiatives face massive operational friction when onboarding hundreds of student or micro-influencers. For Chief Financial Officers, payroll specialists, and finance managers, the sudden influx of decentralized creators presents a logistical nightmare. Managing high-volume, low-value payouts domestic and international often forces lean teams into manual wire setups, constant troubleshooting of missing routing details, and endless email chains regarding payment statuses. When hundreds of micro-influencers are actively creating localized content, traditional payment methods cannot keep pace with the speed of digital campaigns. Operational efficiency drops significantly when accounting teams spend hours verifying individual banking details or correcting typo-ridden routing codes. This friction does not just drain internal corporate resources; it actively disincentivizes the young creators who form the backbone of modern grassroots mobilization. The strategy behind voter mobilization has fundamentally shifted because the habits of the electorate have changed. Research published by the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy demonstrates that 69% of next-gen donors and advocates prefer to interact with causes and learn about civic engagement directly through social media influencers rather than traditional organizations. To successfully leverage this shift, organizations must deploy specialized campaign technologies capable of managing decentralized networks, as explored in recent digital organizing analyses by Higher Ground Labs . How Can a Global Payouts API Scale GOTV Campaigns? Scaling a civic campaign through decentralized activism requires a major technological shift in how funds are dispersed. A global payouts API solves this challenge by fully automating the payment lifecycle from initial creator onboarding to the final transaction delivery. Instead of requiring a payroll specialist to manually input transaction data into a banking portal, the platform triggers automated payouts based on verified campaign milestones or content submissions. This automation abstracts hyper-localized payment routing by serving as an intelligent switchboard between various financial networks. When a student or micro-influencer completes a targeted outreach task, the API determines the most efficient path to deliver the funds based on the recipient's geographic location and preferred payout channel. This operational agility allows organizations to instantly process payouts across diverse payment networks like Venmo, PayPal, ACH, and local international rails through a single corporate integration. By shifting the operational burden away from internal finance teams, the organization can scale its influencer network from dozens to thousands without adding administrative headcount. The system automatically validates data before any money moves, minimizing the risk of failed transactions due to incorrect banking details. This level of efficiency ensures that micro-influencers receive their compensation instantly, which builds long-term campaign loyalty and keeps digital activism momentum high. What are the Compliance Risks of Paying Micro-Influencers for Civic Engagement? Operating high-volume digital campaigns within the United States requires strict adherence to federal and state tax regulations. Onboarding hundreds of short-term contractors introduces substantial regulatory compliance risks, particularly concerning identity verification and annual tax reporting. If an organization fails to collect accurate tax documentation before distributing funds, it faces severe financial penalties from the Internal Revenue Service. A modern global payouts API mitigates these compliance risks by embedding automated documentation collection directly into the creator onboarding flow. The system handles several critical compliance tasks automatically: Collecting and validating digital W-9 forms for domestic creators and W-8BEN forms for international participants before any payouts are authorized. Conducting real-time identity verification and global sanctions screening to prevent fraudulent accounts and ensure regulatory compliance. Tracking cumulative payouts over the calendar year and automatically generating, filing, and mailing necessary tax forms when individual thresholds are met. Automating these workflows ensures that your finance department remains audit-ready without requiring manual oversight for every new influencer sign-up. The compliance engine adapts automatically to shifting state and federal regulations, providing a robust layer of risk management that protects the parent organization while maintaining a smooth user experience for the activist network. Why Traditional Payout Methods Fail for High-Volume Activism Campaigns? Relying on legacy payout systems or manual processes creates a severe bottleneck that can stall an entire voter engagement initiative. Traditional corporate banking tools and standard wire transfers are designed for predictable B2B transactions, not for sending thousands of small payments to a fragmented network of gig-economy workers and student creators. When compared to an API-first approach, legacy payment methods present several clear disadvantages: High transaction fees: Standard international wires and legacy contractor management platforms often charge steep flat fees per transaction, which destroys the financial viability of sending low-value payouts to micro-influencers. Rigid payout channels: Traditional systems often force all recipients to use standard bank wires or bank transfers, ignoring the preference of younger demographics who rely heavily on digital wallets and instant mobile money apps. Manual data corrections: Legacy systems lack automated validation, meaning a single incorrect character in a routing number results in a failed payment that requires manual intervention from a payroll specialist to resolve. Balancing Impact and Infrastructure Budgets Managing a growing activist network requires careful budget allocation, and finance leaders cannot afford to overspend on administrative software. Scalable payout platforms recognize this reality by offering transparent, tiered pricing structures that allow organizations to access enterprise-grade automation features without a massive financial commitment. For early-stage initiatives or local campaigns, entry-level tiers provide immediate access to core API functionalities, automated tax collection, and international payout capabilities for a low monthly fee. As the campaign scales and transaction volume grows, the platform easily transitions into high-volume pricing tiers that lower individual transaction fees. This predictable financial model ensures that civic tech platforms can dedicate the vast majority of their budget directly to grassroots impact rather than administrative overhead. Choosing a Secure Partner for Your Influencer Payouts For organizations dedicated to maximizing civic participation through modern digital networks, Dots represents the ideal choice for secure, automated developer-first payouts. Unlike traditional contractor payment platforms that trap your business in rigid financial ecosystems or require tedious manual management, Dots provides a unified payout infrastructure that completely automates global payouts, compliance, and onboarding. The platform enables businesses to send funds to over 190 countries in more than 135 currencies through a single, seamless API integration. By choosing Dots, your finance and development teams gain access to an intelligent routing engine that bypasses the high fees and processing delays associated with legacy systems. Dots eliminates the friction of chasing missing bank details by letting creators choose how they want to get paid, whether through instant digital wallets or local bank rails, all while automatically managing tax forms and identity verification in the background. Partnering with Dots means giving your campaign the operational capability to scale your micro-influencer activism safely, securely, and efficiently. Ready to automate your campaign payouts and streamline your compliance? Talk to us today and see how Dots can help scale your GOTV campaign.

title: Quantum BioPharma Strengthens Equity and Liquidity in Q2 2026 as FDA Approves Lucid-MS for Pivotal Phase 2 Clinical Trial
summary: TORONTO, Aug. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Quantum BioPharma Ltd. (NASDAQ: QNTM) (CSE: QNTM) (FRA: 0K91) (
body_text: TORONTO, Aug. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Quantum BioPharma Ltd. (NASDAQ: QNTM) (CSE: QNTM) (FRA: 0K91) ("Quantum" or the "Company"), has reported its financial and operational results for the second quarter of 2026, ended June 30, 2026. As of June 30, 2026, the Company’s combined cash and cash equivalents, and digital assets, totaled approximately US$9.5 million, an increase from US$4.1 million as of December 31, 2025. Assuming the current cash burn rate for the first half of 2026, management confirms that current liquidity is sufficient to fund planned operations to at least October 2027. Subsequent to quarter-end, the Company received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval to proceed with its Lucid-MS Phase 2 clinical trial in progressive multiple sclerosis, a pivotal regulatory milestone that advances the Company’s patented, first-in-class neuroprotective program into the next stage of clinical development. Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results Quantum delivered another quarter of disciplined execution, materially reducing both operating expenses and cash burn year-over-year while strengthening its treasury and overall balance sheet. Liquidity and Balance Sheet Strength Combined cash, cash equivalents, and digital assets of approximately US$9.5 million as of June 30, 2026, increased from US$4.1 million as of December 31, 2025. Cash and cash equivalents nearly doubled to US$3.65 million, up from US$1.91 million at December 31, 2025. Total shareholders’ equity increased to US$6.09 million, up approximately 19% from US$5.10 million at December 31, 2025, reflecting a strengthened capital base. Working capital improved significantly to approximately US$1.66 million as of June 30, 2026, up from approximately US$0.42 million at December 31, 2025, driven by the stronger cash and digital asset position. Key Financial Ratios (as of June 30, 2026) Current ratio of 1.2 as of June 30, 2026, compared to 1.07 as of December 31, 2025, indicating strengthened short-term liquidity and full coverage of near-term obligations. Quick ratio of 1.19 as of June 30, 2026, compared to 1.06 as of December 31, 2025 (current assets excluding inventory and prepaid expenses, divided by current liabilities), confirming robust liquidity even on a conservative basis. Debt-to-Equity ratio of 1.36 as of June 30, 2026, compared to 1.19 as of December 31, 2025. Importantly, approximately 47% of current liabilities, as of June 30, 2026, are associated with non-cash derivative fair value items, reflecting the Company’s strong balance sheet management. Reduced Cash Burn and Cost Discipline Total operating expenses decreased by 53% in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, to US$2.29 million from US$4.85 million. General and administrative expenses decreased by 47% in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, to US$1.76 million from US$3.31 million. Cash used in operating activities fell 44% to US$3.46 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, down from US$6.21 million in the same period of 2025, building on the reduction trend established in the first quarter. Second Quarter & Subsequent 2026 Corporate Highlights United States FDA Clearance to Proceed with Lucid-MS Phase 2 Trial in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis Subsequent to quarter-end, on August 10, 2026, the Company announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had approved its Investigational New Drug (IND) application for Lucid-MS (Lucid-21-302), clearing the Company to advance its patented, first-in-class multiple sclerosis program into a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with progressive MS, an area of substantial unmet medical need within a global MS therapeutics market anticipated to reach approximately US$38.62 billion by 2030 (Grand View Research, 2026). Management Commentary "FDA clearance to proceed with our Lucid-MS Phase 2 trial is a transformative moment for Quantum and the result of years of dedicated scientific research," said Zeeshan Saeed, Chief Executive Officer of Quantum. “We brought total operating expenses down by more than 50% year-over-year in the second quarter, and our strengthened financial position assuming cash burn rate similar to the first half of 2026 provides a runway to at least October 2027 at our current budgeted spend," said Donal Carroll, Chief Financial Officer of Quantum. About Quantum BioPharma Ltd. Quantum is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to building a portfolio of innovative assets and biotech solutions for the treatment of challenging neurodegenerative and metabolic disorders and alcohol misuse disorders with drug candidates in different stages of development. Through its wholly owned subsidiary, Lucid Psycheceuticals Inc. ("Lucid"), Quantum is focused on the research and development of its lead compound, Lucid-MS. Lucid-MS is a patented new chemical entity shown to prevent and reverse myelin degradation, the underlying mechanism of multiple sclerosis, in preclinical models. Quantum invented UNBUZZD™ and spun out its OTC version to a company, Unbuzzd Wellness Inc. ("Unbuzzd") (formerly, Celly Nutrition Corp.), led by industry veterans. Quantum retains ownership of 19.48% (as of June 30, 2026) of Unbuzzd at www.unbuzzd.com . The agreement with Unbuzzd also includes royalty payments of 7% of sales from unbuzzd™ until payments to Quantum total $250 million. Once $250 million is reached, the royalty drops to 3% in perpetuity. Quantum retains 100% of the rights to develop similar products or alternative formulations specifically for pharmaceutical and medical uses. title: Alvotech Announces Financial Results for the First Half of 2026 and Provides a Business Update
summary: REYKJAVIK, ICELAND (August 19, 2026) — Alvotech (NASDAQ: ALVO; ALVO-SDB) (“Alvotech” or the “Company”), a global biotechnology company specializing in the development and manufacture of biosimilar medicines for patients worldwide, today announced financial results for the first half of 2026 and
body_text: REYKJAVIK, ICELAND (August 19, 2026) — Alvotech (NASDAQ: ALVO; ALVO-SDB) (“Alvotech” or the “Company”), a global biotechnology company specializing in the development and manufacture of biosimilar medicines for patients worldwide, today announced financial results for the first half of 2026 and provided a business update. A supplemental long‑form earnings release and management presentation providing additional details and business update is available on our website: https://alvotech.com/financials .1 H1 2026 financial highlights Adjusted total revenue2 was $211.9 million compared to $306.1 million in the same period last year. Gross Margin of 54% was broadly level with the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA2 was $46.9 million compared to $53.7 million in the same period last year. Cash-balance at the end of the period was $142.8 million compared to $172.4 million on December 31, 2025. USD millions – adjusted financial measures2 H1 2026 H1 2025 Change % Product and Service Revenue 105.9 204.7 -48.3% License and Other Revenue 105.7 101.4 4.4% Other Income 0.2 0.1 49.7% Total revenue 211.9 306.1 -30.8% Gross margin 54% 55% EBITDA 46.9 53.7 -12.7% Q2 2026 business highlights Alvotech resubmitted US Biologics License Applications for AVT05, proposed biosimilar to Simponi® and Simponi Aria® and AVT06, proposed biosimilar to Eylea®, following the comprehensive responses to the US Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) Post-Application Action Letter (PAAL). Alvotech’s partner, Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, resubmitted the US Biologics License Application for AVT03, proposed biosimilar to Prolia®/Xgeva®. FDA confirmed review completion goal dates in alignment with the standard 6-month process, with decisions anticipated in the fourth quarter of 2026. FDA closed its inspection of the company’s manufacturing facility in Reykjavik, conducted in April-May 2026, and confirmed a VAI classification. Alvotech closed an underwritten public offering and private placement, generating gross proceeds of approximately $165 million that will be used for continued pipeline development, working capital and general corporate purposes. Liquidity was further strengthened by a new term loan facility of $75 million with funds managed by GoldenTree Asset Management LP. Comments by Lisa Graver, CEO: “During the first half, we continued to advance our strategic priorities, including significant improvements to our manufacturing facility and quality systems. This work enabled the resubmission in June of our U.S. applications for AVT05 and AVT06 alongside our partner’s resubmission of AVT03. This was an important inflection point as we work towards FDA approvals in the fourth quarter of 2026. The FDA also formally closed its recent routine cGMP surveillance inspection of our facility with a VAI classification. “We have also continued to advance our pipeline, including the FDA acceptance of our BLA for AVT16, our proposed interchangeable biosimilar to Entyvio, and validation by the EMA of the European applications for AVT16 and AVT80. We believe we are well positioned for the next wave of product launches. “The manufacturing improvement program affected output and product availability during the first half, which was reflected in our revenues and adjusted EBITDA. Manufacturing returned to planned operating levels at the end of the second quarter, and we are building supply to meet confirmed demand. We expect this to support strengthening financial performance as we move through the second half of the year. Importantly, underlying commercial demand for products remains strong, both in the U.S. and Europe. “We enter the second half with five biosimilars now contributing to product revenue, and important regulatory catalysts ahead. The strong support received from existing and new investors in our recent equity financing, together with the new term loan facility, further strengthens our financial position as we execute on the significant opportunities that lie ahead.” Outlook for 2026 full year Management anticipates total revenues to be in the range of $650-$700 million and adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $180-220 million in 2026. All materials for the webcast are available at https://alvotech.com/financials . An earnings call is held on the following day, after release of the results. Please note that all dates are subject to change. Quarter Date of release Date of earnings call Q3 2026 November 11, 2026 November 12, 2026 Q4 2026 March 10, 2027 March 11, 2027 About Alvotech Alvotech is a biotechnology company, founded by Robert Wessman, focused solely on the development and manufacture of biosimilar medicines for patients worldwide. Alvotech seeks to be a global leader in the biosimilar space by delivering high-quality, cost-effective products and services, enabled by a fully integrated approach and broad in-house capabilities. title: Klaviyo Composer and Agencies: The Case for Working Together - Klaviyo
summary: Klaviyo Composer builds campaigns in minutes from your own data. Agencies bring proven insight across brands AI alone can't surface. Why you need both.
body_text: Composer speeds things up. Agencies know what's actually worth speeding up. Generated by Klaviyo AI Klaviyo Composer compresses creative production from days to minutes, pulling from your own account data and patterns across 193,000+ brands. But that data reflects the average, not the exception, which is where a specialized agency's tested playbook comes in. Composer handles speed and implementation: It's built into Klaviyo and draws on 14+ years of aggregate marketing intelligence to turn hours of production work into minutes. Benchmarks show the middle of the pack, not the top of it: Composer's data spans every account type, underperformers included, so it can't isolate what separates good results from great ones. Agencies test the moves an algorithm wouldn't suggest: Reframing billing reminders as gifting moments, or sending plain-text emails instead of designed ones, are wins the author found only by testing across many accounts. The value is in cross-account pattern recognition: Agencies can answer "how do other brands like us solve this," a question that requires seeing what's working across a curated set of top performers. The two are meant to work together: Composer drives speed and volume; an agency brings the strategic judgment on what to test and why, so brands get both breadth and depth. Sign up Get a demo Klaviyo Composer is a genuine breakthrough for marketing teams. What used to take days (briefing, building, copy review, quality assurance checks, etc.) can now happen in minutes, grounded in your own account data and backed by 14+ years of Klaviyo's marketing intelligence across 193,000+ brands. That's an incredibly meaningful shift in how fast brands can move. So why, in a world where AI can produce ready-made creative on demand, would a brand still need an agency? In my role as founder and CEO of YOCTO Agency , a boutique lifecycle marketing agency and Klaviyo Elite partner, I've been thinking about this a lot. If you manage brands on Klaviyo, or if you’re a Klaviyo brand considering hiring an agency, I’m sure you have, too. I've been part of conversations with Klaviyo's leadership about the direction of AI for at least a year, and I've been watching our own agency go through the shift in real time. My honest take: tools like Composer don't make agencies irrelevant. They change what agencies are actually for. What Composer does really well Composer is Klaviyo's AI orchestration layer built natively into the platform. It sees inside your account: your flows, campaigns, segments, customer behavior, and historical performance. That means with Composer, you have two powerful data layers working for you: Your own performance history Aggregate patterns across the broader Klaviyo ecosystem That combination is powerful. Composer can take a task that used to require hours of production time and compress that timeline dramatically. It can surface patterns you might not have noticed in your own data. It can help you implement faster and more consistently. But here's the thing: both of those data layers are bound by what's already inside your account, and by what's average across the accounts Klaviyo can see. The third data layer Klaviyo benchmarks are incredibly useful. They tell you how you perform relative to businesses like yours. But "businesses like yours" includes everyone: the underperformers, the average, and the exceptional. The benchmark reflects the middle of the distribution, not the top of it. An agency that's worked deeply in your industry has something different: a curated dataset drawn specifically from top-performing accounts. Not what's normal, but what's actually working at the highest level. And more importantly, why . At YOCTO Agency, we work exclusively with health and wellness brands on subscription-based business models. That focus means that when a client comes to us with a specific problem (e.g., subscribers canceling, payment recovery rates dropping, psychographic segmentation they don't know how to implement), we're never starting from scratch. We've seen this exact problem before, across many accounts, and we've measured what actually moves the needle. This is the kind of expertise that only an agency can bring to the table. An agency that's worked deeply in your industry has something different: a curated dataset drawn specifically from top-performing accounts. What agency expertise looks like in practice Let me give you a couple of concrete examples. Billing reminders vs. gifting moments One of the most common cancellation drivers for subscription brands is the billing reminder. You know the one: "You're about to be charged $X. Your next shipment includes Y." It's accurate. It's transactional. But it triggers cancellations at a surprisingly high rate. What we discovered, after testing this across multiple clients, is that reframing those notifications as gifting moments changes the dynamic significantly. Instead of telling a subscriber they're about to be charged, you tell them something they're about to receive. The psychology shifts from obligation to anticipation, and cancellation rates drop meaningfully. That insight doesn’t come from a benchmark. It comes from running the test, measuring the result, and doing it again with enough accounts to be confident in the pattern. That’s the kind of practice any agency worth hiring is doing regularly. The one-line plaint-text email The best LLMs and vibe marketing tools probably won’t tell you to send a plain-text email without any bells or whistles. But in my experience, plain-text email significantly outperforms every designed, fully-branded alternative. We know this because we’ve tested. The simpler the message, the more it reads like a real person reaching out, and the more people respond to it. An LLM isn’t likely to surface this insight because it goes against conventional wisdom. You'd have to be willing to test it, and you'd have to have enough context across enough accounts to trust what the data is telling you. Again, this is exactly the expertise an agency should bring to the table. The questions brands actually ask Here's the pattern I see most often. A brand comes to us and says something like: "We want to increase our subscription take rate. What's the best structure for our offering?" "We're seeing a lot of chargebacks and we don't know how to combat this." "We want to introduce psychographic personalization, but we don't have the capability, and we're not even sure how to measure whether it worked." These aren't questions any AI tool can answer on its own, because it can't see what the best brands in your category are doing. The most valuable question we get at YOCTO Agency, over and over, is some version of: "How do other clients of yours solve this?" And we’re not alone. “Half our value is just being able to share how other brands have handled a particular problem,” says Zac Fromson, co-founder of Lilo Social , a full-funnel growth agency. “That cross-account memory is the thing brands are really paying for right now.” It’s this type of question that requires that third data layer. The right frame: both, not either/or The play here isn't Composer or agency. It's Composer and agency. Composer handles the speed and implementation side beautifully. It should. That's exactly what it's built for. What an agency offers is the strategic layer on top: the frameworks developed from working with many brands like yours, the out-of-the-box tests you'd never think to run on your own, and the ability to look at your situation and say, with confidence, here's what's actually likely to move the needle, and here's how we know. Think of it this way. Benchmarks give you a wide view across many accounts, and Composer gives you depth inside your own account. An agency that specializes in your category can give you both: wide coverage across comparable accounts, and real depth into what separates good performance from great. Brands that pair AI-powered orchestration with that kind of human-curated intelligence get the best of both worlds. The efficiency gains from Composer are real. So is the strategic gap that a great agency partner fills. “Speed without direction just means faster mistakes,” Paul Pritchard, group CEO of Overdose , a global digital commerce consultancy specializing in end-to-end retail and B2B solutions. “Agencies provide the architectural judgment from years of cross-industry experience that machines simply can’t replicate.” Agencies provide the architectural judgment from years of cross-industry experience that machines simply can't replicate. Paul Pritchard Group CEO, Overdose What this means for how agencies need to evolve You already know: the cost of producing content is heading toward zero. If implementation, output, and volume are the main things your agency is selling, that's going to be a tough position to defend. “The agencies that will matter moving forward will be those that use AI to accelerate delivery while partnering entirely around measurable business outcomes,” says Pritchard. That’s because they’ve built something an AI genuinely can't replicate: proprietary frameworks tested across real accounts, in specific categories over real time. These are the agencies that will be able to walk into a client conversation and say, "Here's what we've seen work for businesses exactly like yours, and here's the data behind it." “A model can produce the asset,” Fromson says. “But it doesn’t have the scar tissue an agency does.” A model can produce an asset, but it doesn't have the scar tissue an agency does. Zac Fromson Co-founder, Lilo Social Agencies have perspectives AI can’t produce on its own. And for brands that want to operate at the top of their category rather than the middle of the pack, that's exactly what they should be looking for in a partner. George Kapernaros George Kapernaros is the founder of YOCTO, a cutting-edge marketing agency specialising in email, mobile, and direct mail strategies for some of the world's fastest-scaling brands across diverse sectors, like health and wellness, beauty, and luxury goods. In less than 2 years, not only has the agency partnered with top brands like Kilo.health, BetterMe, Evereden, Healf, and Dandelion Chocolate, but was also handpicked to join Klaviyo's Partner Advisory Council (PAC), achieving Platinum Partner status within its first year. Before founding YOCTO, George served as marketing director at Divbrands, where he helped bootstrap the company to 8-figure revenue profitably in 3 years. He holds a degree in Political Science, is currently pursuing an MBA at Quantic, and is an instructor at CXL. Currently based in Athens, Greece, George believes that creativity is the ultimate business superpower. title: How to Become a CNA: A Step-by-Step Guide
summary: See each step to becoming a CNA, from eligibility requirements to certification to registration, plus what to expect in terms of cost and timeline.
body_text: Becoming a certified nursing assistant (CNA) is one of the fastest ways to start a career in healthcare. CNA training is designed to get you from application to paycheck in months rather than years, making it much faster than becoming an LPN or RN. CNAs are regulated by state and federal government rules, and each state has its own specifics for training and registration. However, the path to becoming a CNA follows the same basic pattern no matter where you live. In some states, there are basic eligibility requirements like having a high school diploma/GED or being a certain age. You then have to complete a CNA training program and pass an exam. Finally, you’ll get listed on a state registry. The exact hours, costs, and paperwork differ by state, but the steps themselves are the same. Since free or employer-paid training options exist in most areas, the cost to becoming a CNA is often much lower than similar healthcare roles. This guide walks you through each step of becoming a CNA, from eligibility requirements to certification to registration. We’ll also cover what to expect in terms of cost, timeline, and life after certification. How to Become a CNA Here's what the process looks like to become a CNA, from meeting basic requirements to getting listed on your state's registry. Step 1: Meet the Basic Eligibility Requirements Before you can work as a CNA, you need to meet some basic qualifications in some states. These are eligibility requirements set by the state that you need to meet before enrolling in a training program. There are also requirements set by your training provider, the clinical site where you will learn hands-on skills, and your future employer. So, some apply when you enroll, while others apply when you begin working. If you look at job postings , you’ll see that some employers may require a TB test. Others may require CPR certification. The specifics depend on the employer and work setting. Common requirements to enroll in a training program While requirements vary by state, here are some common examples: Meet the minimum age requirement, usually 16 to 18 depending on the state A high school diploma or GED (though not all states require this) Pass any required criminal background screening Certain basic health screenings and proof of vaccinations, to clear you for the clinical placement built into your program Common requirements to work as a CNA These may be required by your state when you apply to be on the state registry, or by your employer before you can begin working. Government-issued identification Proof you are authorized to work in the U.S. Specific health screenings and vaccinations CPR certification Drug screening Step 2: Complete a State-Approved CNA Training Program Nursing assistants need to complete a state-approved training program that includes academic coursework and hands-on clinical training before they can take their state’s competency exam. A few states offer alternate pathways to the exam, but it’s not the norm. Federal law states that in order for a training program to be approved by the state, it must include at least 75 hours of instruction . This must include at least 16 hours of supervised practical training. Some states require more, ranging from 75 to 180 hours of instruction. Programs typically take 4 to 12 weeks to complete, depending on whether you attend full-time or part-time. The classroom topics cover things like infection control, safety and emergency procedures, and respecting patients' rights. From there, training moves into hands-on skills like taking vital signs, bathing and dressing, feeding and toileting assistance, and safely transferring and repositioning patients. There are also specialized topics like caring for cognitively impaired patients. Where to take CNA classes CNA training is widely available, so you likely have several options nearby, including: Community colleges and vocational schools Online programs that pair virtual coursework with in-person clinical hours Hospitals and nursing homes that train their own staff Job Corps centers Approved community organizations How much CNA training costs CNA programs typically cost anywhere from $1,000 to $2,000 from an online provider or community college. They can run several thousand dollars more at a private vocational school. The price depends on your state, the program length, and whether it's public or private. On top of tuition, extras like background checks, immunizations, uniforms that might be required for clinical settings, and your exam fee can add a few hundred dollars more. The good news is that there are many free CNA training programs available. Nursing home training and reimbursement: Nursing homes generally cover CNA training and testing costs for nurse aides they employ or have offered employment. You may also qualify for reimbursement if you complete approved training elsewhere and are hired by a qualifying nursing facility within 12 months. ‍ Employer-sponsored training: Many nursing homes and hospitals pay for your CNA training if you commit to working for them afterward. ‍ Job Corps: This free federal program offers CNA training to eligible young adults ages 16 to 24. ‍ Local workforce development boards: Many communities offer tuition assistance for approved healthcare training through American Job Centers . Keep in mind that "free" usually covers tuition only. You may still owe money for books, uniforms, or your exam fee, so ask upfront exactly what's included. Step 3: Pass the CNA Certification Exam Once training is complete, you'll apply to take the state competency exam. You may have to complete basic state requirements at that time, like fingerprinting or providing a background check. CNA competency exams typically include a written test and a hands-on skills evaluation, although the components you must complete can depend on your state. For example, Florida has both a written portion and clinical skills evaluation, but if you’ve passed an approved training program in the past six months, you don’t have to take the clinical skills portion. Here’s a look at how each of the components works: A written portion: The written test has 60 multiple-choice questions that evaluate nursing assistant knowledge and skills. You have 90 minutes to take the test. There is a list of topics available as well as practice exams. A clinical skills evaluation: This is a timed test that will ask you to perform five nursing assistant skills in front of two nurses. Three of the skills are randomly chosen, and the other two are Handwashing and Indirect Care. You must show competency in all five skills to pass. Other states follow a similar format, though the exact number of questions and skills can vary. CNA exams don't necessarily use a standard percentage, such as 70%, as the passing score. States select their own passing standard, but many do not publish it. Florida, to continue our example, says that you have to pass all five of the skills but does not publish the passing standard for the written exam. If you fail, you'll usually get another chance. In Florida, you have up to three attempts to pass the exam. After three failed attempts, you must complete an approved training program before testing again. Tips for passing the CNA skills test Here are some ways to prepare for the CNA skills test: Practice the entire skill from start to finish, even if some of the parts seem very easy. This will help you remember every step. Narrate your actions out loud, since evaluators often listen for safety steps like hand hygiene. Time yourself so you're comfortable working within the time limit. Review your state's official skills list ahead of time, and practice all the skills listed, even if you think they are easy. If you make a mistake, keep calm and continue. You need to achieve competency, not perfection. Step 4: Get Listed on Your State's Nurse Aide Registry In most states, being listed on the state’s nurse aide registry is required to legally work as a CNA. This registry confirms that your certification is active and lets employers verify your credentials before hiring you. Typically, the organization that gives the exam sends your results directly to the state. Processing time varies, but many states add your name within a few days to a couple of weeks of receiving your passing results. Some states issue a physical certificate or ID card, while others rely entirely on an online, searchable registry. Either way, keep a copy of your certification for your own records. As with other requirements we’ve discussed, this varies by state. For example, federal nursing-home rules let some aides work while completing approved training or awaiting registry listing, generally up to four months. Learn About Our Healthcare Career Training for Caregivers Explore Programs How Long Does It Take to Become a CNA? Altogether, most people can become a CNA in 6 weeks to 6 months, broken down roughly like this: Training program: These take anywhere from 4 to 12 weeks, depending on whether you attend full-time or part-time. Exam scheduling and results: This typically takes an additional 1 to 4 weeks, depending on the state and testing vendor. In Florida, for example, your exam is scheduled within 7 to 14 business days, and results are returned within 72 hours. Registry listing: This can take from a few business days to a few weeks after you pass, depending on your state. Most will tell you what to expect. Allow extra time if you need to reschedule your exam or wait on something like background check results. Because timelines vary so much by state and by your own schedule, you should consider these numbers as rough estimates and check your state requirements and timeline to get a true idea of how long it’ll take you to become a CNA. How CNA Requirements Vary by State Every state sets its own training hours, minimum age, exam vendor, and renewal timeline, so requirements can look pretty different depending on where you live. For example, state-by-state requirements show Iowa and Indiana require the federal minimum of 75 hours of training, while Connecticut requires at least 100 hours and Maine requires 180. Florida stands out because some applicants can qualify for certification without completing a formal CNA training program. Because of this range, check your state's board of nursing or health department page for the exact requirements before you enroll in a program. Keeping Your CNA Certification Active CNA certification isn't permanent. Most states require renewal every 24 months, and the process is usually simple if you've stayed employed as a CNA. Most states require you to perform some paid nursing or nursing-related work during each renewal period to keep your registry status active. The exact work and continuing-education requirements vary by state. If you didn't work during that time, expect a more involved process, which could include retraining or passing a competency exam again. Check your state's specific rules well before your certification expires. What Happens After You're Certified? Once you're certified, you can start looking for a job in the setting that appeals to you most. That may be a hospital, nursing home, or private home doing home healthcare. Each setting has a different pace and patient load, so it's worth thinking about which environment suits your working style before you apply. Many CNAs use this role to build experience before pursuing further education, like enrolling in an LPN or RN program. Many LPN and RN programs view CNA experience as a plus, since it shows comfort with hands-on patient care. Alternatively, some CNAs add optional certifications, like phlebotomy or EKG monitoring. These may help if you decide to move on to another role, like a patient care technician or medical assistant . These add-on certifications typically take just a few weeks to complete and can lead to expanded duties and higher pay. Whichever direction you choose, the experience you gain as a CNA will help. Employers value experience with hands-on patient care and being part of a healthcare team. >> Read More: CNA vs. Patient Care Technician or CNA vs. Medical Assistant FAQs on How to Become a CNA What are the minimum requirements to become a CNA? Requirements vary by state and training program. Common requirements include meeting a minimum age, passing background screening, completing a state-approved training program, and passing the state competency exam. Some states or programs also require a high school diploma or GED. How much does CNA training cost? Programs typically range from $1,000 to $2,000 at community colleges to a few thousand dollars more at private schools. However, there are many free training options through employers, Medicare- or Medicaid-certified facilities, or workforce development programs. Can I become a CNA online? In-person clinical training is required by the federal government . So, some CNA programs offer academic coursework online, but every program will still require an in-person component. Do I need a high school diploma to become a CNA? It depends on the state and training program. Some require a high school diploma or GED, while others have lower education requirements or none at all. Check your state's requirements and the admission requirements for the program you're considering. How many times can I retake the CNA exam if I fail? Each state has its own rules about retaking the exam. In Florida , you have up to three attempts to pass the exam. After three failed attempts, you must complete an approved training program before testing again. Check with your state's board of nursing or health department. Is CNA training free? There are many free options. Nursing homes generally cover CNA training and testing costs for nurse aides they employ or have offered employment. You may also qualify for reimbursement if you complete approved training elsewhere and are hired by a qualifying nursing facility within 12 months. There are also employer-sponsored programs , Job Corps , and workforce development programs. Can I transfer my CNA certification to another state? Probably. Each state maintains its own Nurse Aide Registry, so you'll usually need to apply for reciprocity or certification in your new state, which may include extra paperwork or a new competency exam. Can I work while waiting for my CNA exam or registry listing? It depends on your state, employer, and where you work. Some nursing facilities can employ nurse aides who are still completing approved training or waiting to be added to the registry, subject to federal and state requirements. Check your state's rules before starting work. Does CNA certification expire if I stop working? Yes. If you don't meet your state's minimum work-hour requirement during the renewal period, usually every 24 months, your certification can lapse. You may need to retrain or retest to reactivate it. How is a CNA different from a home health aide (HHA)? CNAs typically work in facilities like nursing homes as part of a larger care team, while HHAs mostly work one-on-one with clients in private homes. That is the biggest difference, but HHAs and CNAs also have different training requirements, duties, and salaries. Could becoming a medical assistant be a good next step after working as a CNA? Becoming a medical assistant is one possible next step for a CNA. MAs and CNAs share some overlapping skills, but medical assistants perform a different mix of administrative and clinical tasks, typically in outpatient settings. body_text: Investors News & Events Press Releases Press Releases Global Payments Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results August 05, 2026 6:55am EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio Presentation PDF Trended Financial Highlights SPREADSHEET Second quarter 2026 GAAP diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.05 and adjusted EPS of $3.46, an increase of 12%. Second quarter 2026 GAAP revenue of $3.32 billion and adjusted net revenue of $3.16 billion. On a normalized basis1, adjusted net revenue increased 4%. Updates 2026 outlook and reaffirms 2026 capital return plan. $1.2 billion of capital returned to shareholders year-to-date. ATLANTA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Global Payments Inc. (NYSE: GPN) today announced results for the second quarter ending June 30, 2026. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805443718/en/ “We delivered solid second quarter results that were consistent with our expectations, reflecting the resilience of our business model amidst the ongoing conflict in the Middle East,” said Cameron Bready, chief executive officer. “I am particularly pleased with the progress that we have made on the integration of Worldpay as we combine our complementary capabilities to better serve clients and partners globally.” Bready continued, “Through consistent execution and a sharp focus on commercial excellence, we continue to capitalize on growth opportunities while further differentiating Global Payments through feature-rich products and distinctive service experiences. This is evidenced by the accelerating adoption of our Genius platform, which continues to gain momentum across the markets we serve. At the same time, we remain at the forefront of innovation by leveraging AI across our ecosystem to enhance our solutions, elevate customer experiences, and drive greater operational efficiency, further strengthening our competitive position and long-term growth prospects.” Bready concluded, “We are pleased to have returned $1.2 billion in capital to shareholders year-to-date, exceeding 50% of our more than $2 billion plan for 2026, and we remain on track to return approximately $7.5 billion over the 2025 to 2027 time period.” Second Quarter 2026 Summary GAAP revenues were $3.32 billion and diluted earnings per share were $0.05. Adjusted net revenues increased approximately 34% to $3.16 billion. On a normalized basis1, consistent with our full-year outlook, adjusted net revenue increased approximately 4%. Adjusted operating margin expanded 70 basis points on a normalized basis1 to 42.0%. Adjusted EPS increased 12% to $3.46. 2026 Outlook “Our second quarter financial results were consistent with expectations and marked our first full quarter operating as a pure-play commerce solutions provider,” said Josh Whipple, chief financial officer. “Our performance further validates the importance of our scale and distribution and our ability to deliver sustainable growth, margin expansion, and free cash flow.” Whipple continued, “Given the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and its impact on our travel portfolio, we now expect normalized1, constant currency adjusted net revenue growth of approximately 4% – 5% and adjusted earnings per share of $13.60 – $13.80 for the full year. We continue to expect normalized1 adjusted operating margin expansion of approximately 150 basis points for the full year and to return more than $2 billion of capital to shareholders in 2026.” _______________________________ 1 Normalized comparisons include the pre-acquisition results of Worldpay and exclude the results of Issuer Solutions and other divested businesses. Capital Allocation Global Payments’ Board of Directors approved a dividend of $0.25 per share payable on September 25, 2026 to shareholders of record as of September 11, 2026. Conference Call Global Payments’ management will host a live audio webcast today, August 5, 2026, at 8:00 a.m. ET to discuss financial results and business highlights. The audio webcast, along with supplemental financial information, can be accessed via the investor relations page of the company’s website at investors.globalpayments.com. A replay of the audio webcast will be archived on the company's website following the live event. Non-GAAP Financial Measures Global Payments supplements its reporting of revenue, operating income, operating margin, net income attributable to Global Payments, earnings per share, free cash flow, and free cash flow conversion with certain non-GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP financial measures include adjusted revenue, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted net income attributable to Global Payments, adjusted earnings per share, adjusted free cash flow, and adjusted free cash flow conversion. The constant currency growth measures adjust for the impact of exchange rates and are calculated using average exchange rates during the comparable period in the prior year. We believe these non-GAAP financial measures assist investors with evaluating the performance of our business. Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures to focus on the factors that it believes are relevant to managing our business, operations, and performance. Any non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in context with our reporting in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for GAAP measures. Reconciliation of each non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable GAAP measure is included in the schedules to this release, except for forward-looking measures where a reconciliation to the corresponding GAAP measures is not available due to the variability, complexity and limited visibility of the items that are excluded from the non-GAAP outlook measures. The company is unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information. About Global Payments Global Payments Inc. (NYSE: GPN) is a leading payment technology and software company that powers commerce for businesses of all sizes worldwide. We help businesses grow with confidence by delivering innovative solutions that enable seamless payment acceptance, smarter operations and exceptional client experiences – online, in store and everywhere in between. With its global reach, local expertise and scale, Global Payments® manages trillions in payments volume and billions of transactions across more than 175 countries. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Global Payments is a Fortune 500® company and a member of the S&P 500. Learn more at company.globalpayments.com.
